Title: Decision Support Analyst
Description:
Requisition ID: 46744

Organization

Vancouver is consistently ranked as one of the world’s most liveable and environmentally sustainable cities. Recognized among BC’s Top Employers and Canada’s Greenest Employers, the City of Vancouver is seeking colleagues who can help advance our core commitments to exceptional public service, sustainability, equity, and an outstanding quality of life for all residents.

With a strong commitment to being a City of Reconciliation, we invite you to join our dedicated team and become part of an innovative, inclusive, and engaging workplace. A career with the City of Vancouver and within the broader public service, offers meaningful work where you play a key role in ensuring equitable access to services, upholding ethical governance, and supporting the needs of citizens with integrity and dedication.

Main Purpose and Function

The Decision Support Analyst is part of the City’s Centre of Expertise for Performance Measurement and Decision Support, within the Strategy and Project Support Office (SPSO). The role supports evidence-informed decision-making across the City by helping leaders understand service performance, assess options, evaluate outcomes, and identify opportunities to improve accountability, transparency and value for money.

The role combines performance measurement, service evaluation, business analysis and business intelligence to help leaders make sound strategic, operational and service-delivery decisions. A core part of the team’s mandate is enabling the delivery of an enterprise-wide corporate planning process and the evaluation of City services, ensuring decisions are grounded in consistent, comparable evidence.

The analysis considers operational, financial, resource and service-delivery implications and supports recommendations to managers and senior leaders.

The Decision Support Analyst partners closely with corporate and departmental teams to build a culture of data-informed decision-making across the City. This includes increasing data literacy, enabling data exploration, supporting adoption of business intelligence tools, and translating complex analysis into clear, decision-ready insight.

Specific Duties/Responsibilities


Performance Measurement and Corporate Planning
Supports performance measurement reporting by linking City services and service plans to performance metrics, departmental work plans and the corporate plan.
Supports the design and delivery of the City’s enterprise-wide corporate planning process, helping connect service plans, performance measures and corporate priorities.
Supports corporate, capital and service-planning processes by connecting service plans and performance information to operating requirements, costs and resource implications.
Develops, monitors and analyzes performance metrics and benchmarks to assess the efficiency, effectiveness and outcomes of City services.
Helps identify short-term and long-term measures that support continuous improvement, service planning and corporate accountability.
Reviews and analyzes how major City decisions may affect service plans, performance measures and service-delivery outcomes.


Service Evaluation and Decision Support


Contributes to the evaluation of City services by helping define evaluation questions, identify measures of success, gather evidence, analyze outcomes and summarize findings.
Synthesizes quantitative and qualitative evidence into clear findings, implications and options for decision-makers.
Provides analytical decision support, including business analysis, options analysis, scenario modelling and business case development, and develops findings and recommendations for managers and senior leaders.
Analyzes and develops service proposals and business cases, including their operating, financial, resource, risk, benefit and performance implications.
Assists client departments in identifying opportunities to improve service outcomes, strengthen accountability, increase transparency and support value-for-money decision-making.
Applies structured problem-solving approaches to complex business, operational and service-delivery questions.


Analytics, Reporting and Data Quality


Develops and maintains datasets, reports, dashboards and analytical models using tools such as Power BI, Excel, SQL and other business intelligence platforms.
Supports the development of user-friendly reporting products that help leaders and service owners understand performance, trends, risks and opportunities.
Works with client departments to identify and remediate data quality issues that affect reporting, analysis and decision-making.
Supports the team’s use of modern analytics platforms, including Microsoft Fabric, Databricks or similar tools, as required.
Contributes to the development of consistent reporting methods, data definitions and analytical approaches across the City.


Stakeholder Support and BI Adoption


Works with client departments to understand business needs, clarify decision questions and translate those needs into useful analytical products.
Supports adoption of business intelligence tools by developing guidance materials, providing training or coaching, and helping users interpret and apply performance information.
Builds effective working relationships with technical, professional and operational staff across the City.
Presents analysis clearly and appropriately for different audiences, including operational teams, managers and senior leaders.
Supports a culture of data-informed decision-making by helping departments use evidence to understand performance, improve services and make better decisions.
Other duties as assigned.


Minimum Qualification Requirements

Education and Experience:


A relevant master’s degree, such as Business Analytics, Commerce, Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, Public Administration or an MBA, or a professional designation, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience. Examples include a CPA.
Minimum 4–5 years of experience in performance measurement, data analytics, service or program evaluation, business analysis, business intelligence or a related field, ideally in a large, complex organization.


Knowledge, Skills And Abilities


Considerable knowledge of performance metrics, benchmarking and service evaluation, with the ability to link operational and financial measures to service outcomes.
Considerable knowledge of business intelligence, analytics and automation tools to transform data into reliable, user-friendly reporting and decision-support products.
Considerable knowledge of business intelligence and analytics tools such as Power BI, Excel, SQL and data modelling approaches.
Considerable knowledge of designing performance measures, indicators or evaluation approaches that inform strategic, operational or service-delivery decisions.
Ability to support corporate planning, service planning, business planning or enterprise reporting processes.
Ability to systematically frame and breakdown complex issues, opportunities or service questions, and reaches conclusions supported by evidence and sound judgment.
Ability to work with structured data, analytical models, data quality issues and modern BI platforms, with the ability to partner effectively with technical teams.
Ability to turn quantitative and qualitative information into clear findings, implications and recommendations.
Ability to present complex analysis simply and compellingly in writing, verbally and through reports, dashboards and presentations.
Experience supporting multi-stakeholder initiatives and presenting analysis to a range of audiences, including managers and senior leaders.
Ability to focus on accuracy, definitions and analytical detail without losing sight of the broader business or service context.
Ability to approach problem-solving with professional judgment, confidentiality, tact and diplomacy.
Collaborative. Builds effective working relationships with technical, professional, operational and senior management staff across the City.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, projects and deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
Knowledge of Python, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Power Automate or similar analytics, automation or cloud data platforms is an asset

Vancouver, BC

What You’ll Do


Develop and produce program evaluation performance metrics and tools to provide accurate and high quality analysis of key indicators, including outcomes, quality and safety, data standards, in ensuring continuous quality improvement for BC Cancer.
Ensure internal, external and public reporting needs are met by gathering and negotiating reporting requirements from customers and stakeholders, communicating requirements to technical resources and following up with stakeholders regularly to develop and implement an examination process for the final reports.
Analyze operational problems and recommend innovative solutions by critically evaluating information gathered from multiple sources, reconciling conflicts, decomposing high-level information into details, abstracting up from low-level information to a general understanding, distinguishing user requests from the underlying true needs, and driving and challenging business assumptions.
Work in collaboration with program leaders and provincial partners to monitor program plans, measure progress towards goals and objectives, and identify the key factors that account for any deviation from stated goals and objectives.
Identify issues with complex data and takes initiative in working out optimal solutions with appropriate stakeholders to improve accuracy, timelines, coordination and other data issues.
Develop reports, dashboards, presentations and briefing documents for multiple internal and external stakeholders.
Provide health planning, program development, and project management support for new initiatives and business cases. Provide leadership in the development of processes to analyze the functionality and effectiveness of program delivery and recommend improvements.
Keep up-to-date about new initiatives, developments, trends and best practice in evaluation and monitoring through literature reviews and contact with key stakeholders from other organizations. Communicate information and make recommendations to program leaders.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training and experience equivalent to a Master’s degree in Business, Analytics, Health Informatics, Health Sciences, or related discipline plus a minimum of five (5) years of recent experience in complex data analysis, health evaluation, project/program management, preferably in a large, multi-site health care environment.

Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Description

In this role, you will own data analytics projects from beginning to end, and will build reports, compile metrics, and own ad hoc and trend analysis. You will utilize business intelligence tools to analyze data and drive key recommendations. You will work with Talent Acquisition leadership to achieve business objectives and communicate insights to key stakeholders. You will recognize and adopt best practices in reporting and analysis, including data integrity, analysis, validation, and documentation; and drive results in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

You will provide analytical support for various Talent Acquisition programs, and build tools to surface timely, meaningful, and actionable data that will drive proactive decision making. Your analysis will contribute deeply to the development of our strategy and drive impact against our hiring objectives. You will collaborate with subject matter experts across Amazon to work through complex problems and to create unified scalable reporting solutions at an enterprise-wide level. You will have the opportunity to partner with the central HR Information Systems teams as an influencer on their next generation road map.

Key job responsibilities


Collaborate with recruiting operations, data scientists, and business leaders to define business processes and provide analytical support
Leverage code to analyze complex datasets and design, develop and evaluate data transformations to solve specific business problems
Build scalable, efficient, and automated data processes to facilitate customer-facing reporting
Automate TA processes to streamline business operations
Communicate verbally or in writing to business customers / leadership for sharing insights and recommendations
Build dashboards and reports for both recruiting leaders and the businesses they support
Perform complex data analysis across multiple systems to support both scheduled and ad-hoc reporting requests
Mine key performance indicators to discover root causes
Analyze business outcome data in order to identify relationships and trends; incorporate data visualization and statistical analyses

Amazon delights millions of customers around the world, and the Talent Acquisition team enables our business leaders to make informed and effective hiring decisions.

5+ years of professional or military experience
5+ years of SQL experience
Experience in scripting for automation (e.g. Python) and advanced SQL skills.
Experience with theory and practice of design of experiments and statistical analysis of results
Experience with AWS technologies


Preferred Qualifications


Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate between data and business needs
Experience managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership

Title: Senior Research Analyst, Institutional Research & Integrated Planning
Description:
Job Summary

The Senior Research Analyst collects, develops, analyzes, and communicates institutional data and other information to constituents throughout the university, to support and enhance decision making, problem solving, strategic planning, policy development, and institutional self-assessment.

The incumbent conducts and manages the design, implementation, and analysis of quantitative and qualitative research for both internal and external parties. The Senior Research Analyst prepares data, analysis, narrative, and presents results.

The incumbent assists in the creation of Business Intelligence reports and dashboards. The position assumes a senior role in regular and customized reporting, providing training, guidance, and structure to junior staff as necessary, in conjunction with the AVP.

The Senior Research Analyst brings forward proposals for new projects and leads, designs, and conducts all levels of research projects in the department.

Qualifications


Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required from a recognized, post-secondary institution. A post baccalaureate certificate in data analysis or equivalent is also required. A graduate degree in a relevant field is considered an asset.
Minimum of five (5) years’ relevant experience, preferably in a higher education setting.
Skill in data analysis, statistical software applications, and social science and business research methodologies.
Experience in Advanced statistical, analytical and computer programming, preferably within higher education data systems and higher education topics.

Tool development
Develop dynamic pricing tools and models to effectively meet business needs.

Required

Aviso:

The Opportunity:

We're looking to fill an opening for a Business Analytics Specialist to join our Data Science and AI Enablement team.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Data Science and AI Enablement, you will be instrumental in supporting the business analytics functions at Aviso Wealth. Principle responsibilities include updating and distributing Business Analytics reporting and ad-hoc data mining for analysis.

As oneaviso:


We Care - You do the right thing for clients, partners and colleagues. You build trusted relationships, champion service excellence, and contribute to a culture where people feel valued and supported
We Dare -You challenge the status quo with bold ideas and fresh perspectives. You embrace change, seek opportunities to innovate and are comfortable exploring new ways of working
We Share - You collaborate openly and build meaningful relationships. You seek out diverse perspectives, share your knowledge and work together to help colleagues, clients and partners succeed
We Deliver - You take ownership of your work, honour your commitments and focus on delivering meaningful results. You hold yourself accountable and continuously look for ways to improve


What your day looks like:


Produce and distribute business reports for internal and external stakeholders, including ad‑hoc data mining across unstructured and disparate data sources.
Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and documentation of all data, reports, assumptions, and methodologies.
Serve as the Asset Management data steward, working with NEI and other providers to validate and maintain high‑quality source data for the data warehouse.
Partner with third‑party data management teams on schema changes and new solutions, including reviewing business requirements, writing technical specifications, and completing system testing.
Influence cross‑functional teams to prioritize Asset Management needs on the data services roadmap, including enhancements to legacy tools.
Apply prescriptive and predictive analytics to strengthen reporting, surface insights to senior leaders, and translate recommendations into action.
Lead research and experimentation as a squad leader to advance DNA strategy within the AI product roadmap


Requirements

Your experience and skills:


Bachelor's degree in a relevant STEM or business field; 5+ years analytics experience in Business Analytics
Certifications in AI/ML or Data Engineering
Experience utilizing Databricks to enable scalable data solutions that support analytics, reporting, and business insights
Experience in federated analytics environments (preferred)
Skilled with SQL, modern BI tools and large, diverse datasets
Working knowledge of Confluence, Jira, and DevOps practices for tracking and documentation
Highly analytical, detail‑oriented, and strong problem solver
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
Excellent collaboration and stakeholder‑management skills with an ability to anticipate business needs and align analytics with strategic priorities
Clear communicator able to translate complex insights for non‑technical audiences
Canadian Securities Course is an asset
Fluent communication skills in English are required and bilingual skills in French are an asset

At Aviso, you will find a dynamic and inclusive culture that rewards innovation and celebrates success.

Competitive compensation package that rewards and recognizes individual contributions

Matching contributions to our retirement program
Commitment to the continuous improvement of our staff through learning & development and an education assistance program
Regular social events to foster teamwork

Your data may be shared with authorized personnel involved in the recruitment process and retained only as long as necessary to fulfill these purposes or as required by law.

Further information is available on the Privacy link on our Career Page - Privacy Policies

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

No recruiters or agencies, please.

We're building a comprehensive, technology-enabled, client-centric wealth services ecosystem. Our clients include our partners, advisors, and investors. We're a trusted partner for nearly all credit unions across Canada, in addition to a wide range of portfolio managers, investment dealers, insurance and trust companies, and introducing brokers. Our partners depend on Aviso for specific solutions that give them a competitive edge in a rapidly evolving, highly competitive industry. Our investment dealer and mutual fund dealer and our insurance services support thousands of investment advisors. Our asset manager, NEI Investments, specializes in investing responsibly. Our online brokerage, Qtrade Direct Investing®, empowers self-directed investors, and our fully automated investing service, Qtrade Guided Portfolios®, serves investors who prefer a hands-off approach. We're actively seeking new talent to join our mission of delivering a stronger energy future in B.C. Position Overview

The Senior HR Reporting Analyst plays a key role in helping FortisBC better understand and leverage workforce data. As the subject matter expert for HR reporting, workforce analytics, and reporting governance, you will work closely with HR, Finance, Information Systems (IS), HRIS, and business leaders to deliver reporting and insights that support workforce planning, talent initiatives, and operational decision-making.

This role combines analytics, problem solving, and collaboration to enhance reporting capabilities, improve data quality and governance, and drive continuous improvement across HR reporting processes and tools.

In this role, you will:


Lead HR reporting and workforce analytics, including executive, Board and regulatory reporting, delivering data-driven insights that support workforce planning, talent initiatives, and organizational decision-making.
Partner with HR, Finance, IS, HRIS, and business leaders to understand reporting needs, analyze workforce trends, and provide actionable recommendations.
Develop, enhance, and maintain HR reporting solutions and establish reporting standards, data definitions, and quality controls to ensure consistent and reliable workforce reporting.
Identify and resolve data quality issues, reporting gaps and inconsistencies, and recommend improvements to HR reporting processes and data.
Drive continuous improvement by streamlining reporting processes, leveraging reporting and visualization tools, and promoting effective use of workforce data.
Lead reporting and analytics projects, support HR technology initiatives, including system enhancements, upgrades, testing, and implementation of new reporting capabilities.
Coordinate HR-related organizational surveys and reporting requirements.

Title: Specialist Data Integration Data Analytics, Reporting & Evaluation
Description:
Specialist, Data Integration Data Analytics, Reporting & Evaluation

Data Analytics

Vancouver, BC

Reporting to the Lead, Data Architecture and Business Intelligence, the Specialist, Data Integration is responsible for the planning, design, development and management of new and existing data warehouse and analytics solutions related to various PHSA programs and services. Applying a broad range of information technology experience, Data Warehousing (DW), Business Intelligence (BI), and clinical and operational knowledge, the Business Intelligence Specialist works with stakeholders to develop analytical products that meet their analytical, reporting, monitoring, surveillance and evaluation needs. This position plans, designs, and develops BI and analytical solutions, including data Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) processes, data marts, reports and dashboards as part of the overall PHSA Enterprise Data Warehouse. This position ensures the integrity and quality of the data accessible through these solutions, and also manages and maintains the metadata and other product documentations.

What You’ll Do


Architect and implement analytics solutions to develop, enhance and improve analytics and use of data at various PHSA programs and external stakeholders. This includes leading the design, development, documentation and implementation of complex data marts, multidimensional cubes or other semantic models, reports, dashboards and other front-end interfaces.
Architect and implement optimal database schemas and ETL solutions to integrate data from various source systems into integrated linked data marts. Collaborate with other members of the team on conceptual design, development, and implementation of the Enterprise Data Warehouse.
Lead the identification of new data sources and implements data extraction routines from departmental feeder systems. Provide advice and direction on data availability and quality. Consult and problem-solves with feeder departments regarding routine data extracts.
Participate in the development, definition and reporting of performance indicators as related to program operations, access and throughput, for use at the program director and executive level. Liaise on behalf of the agency with external consultants on the provisioning of patient specific data, as well as providing education on analysis and interpretation.
Provide technical expertise in the development of Analytics and Business Intelligence solutions by assessing client needs and requirements, reviewing technical options, determining the design and architecture and leading all levels of the solution development and deployment.
Ensure the designed solutions meet the established architectural, security, and quality standards set by the department by actively engaging peers and lead in design and review processes. Maintain current metadata, definitions and documentation of the solutions.
Maintain familiarity with the latest on-premises and cloud analytics technologies, and an awareness of current clinical and business information system trends and issues. Evaluate and recommend products or methods to deliver analytics and Business Intelligence in an accurate, timely and user friendly manner.
Mentor other developers and team members and provides technical and educational support to end users by developing training materials, delivering training sessions and training trainers.
Represent DARE on committees at various levels with regard to data standards, appropriate usage, availability and quality.


Qualifications

What you bring


A level of education, training, and experience equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Health Information Science, Management Information Systems or a related field, plus 3 to 5 years of recent BI, data warehousing, data modelling or analytics experience. Strong understanding of health care system operations and public and population health concepts is definite asset.
Demonstrated knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples in social and health contexts, including supported by significant knowledge of Indigenous-specific mandates, including clear understanding of and commitment to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination and embed Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility.
Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the historic and ongoing impacts of settler colonialism and systemic racism on Indigenous Peoples within social and health contexts. This includes understanding how these factors contribute to current health disparities and barriers to care. Show a clear commitment to identifying, challenging, and eradicating Indigenous-specific racism and all forms of discrimination impacting equity-deserving groups within health care settings. This involves familiarity and understanding Indigenous Cultural Safety and Humility recognizing personal biases, institutional barriers, engaging in anti-racism education and training and advocating for systemic change.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of legislative obligations and provincial commitments within Data Analytics contexts found in the foundational documents including Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan and Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study - BC Human Rights Code, BC Anti-racism Act and how they intersect across the health care system.


Core Competencies


Brings an understanding of the Indigenous specific racism and the broader systemic racism that exists in the colonial health care structure, and has demonstrated initiatives in breaking down barriers and ensuring a safe environment ensuring a sense of belonging to all and informed by Indigenous Cultural Safety.
Awareness of social, economic, political and historical realities of settler colonialism on Indigenous Peoples and familiarity with addressing Indigenous-specific anti-racism, anti-racism and Indigenous Cultural Safety and foundational documents and legislative commitments (the Declaration Act, the Declaration Action Plan, TRC, IPS, Remembering Keegan, etc.).


Skills & Knowledge


Advanced knowledge, and experience in application of best practices of data standards, database design, data architecture and modelling. Expertise in developing ETL solutions, relational and multi-dimensional databases and data marts. Superior database querying, and query optimization skills using Structured Query Language -preferably T-SQL, MDX or DAX or equivalents. Knowledge of experience with BI and visualizations tools such as Microsoft Power BI, and Tableau, and collaboration solutions such as SharePoint. Proven hands-on experience with standard data warehousing and Business Intelligence tools such as Microsoft SQL Server, Integration Services (SSIS), Analysis Services (SSAS), Reporting Services (SSRS), and related development tools and version control tools, or comparable technologies from other vendors. Working knowledge of big data technologies, data science methods and languages such as (Python, R) and Windows and web application development tools and languages is an asset. High level of expertise in Microsoft Office suite of applications.
Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills with the ability to communicate complex ideas in simple terminology with internal and external contacts. Demonstrated ability to analyze operational problems and recommend innovative solutions. Strong analytical, problem solving and system analysis skills including the ability to comprehend complex large scale health care environment operational issues and related data/information and present information in concise meaningful ways. Customer focused with ability to facilitate and encourage cooperation between professionals from other disciplines. Ability to understand management reporting and statistical concepts. Ability to educate and lead management staff on the importance of using high quality data for decision making, via business intelligence tools and other means. Self-directed and motivated to learn new tools and technology. Ability to work independently with little direct supervision and as a member of a multi-disciplinary team. Excellent time management skills with the ability to organize and prioritize work. Physical ability to perform the duties of the job. Persistence and a positive attitude are essential given the iterative development cycle and sometimes problematic data integration issues.
Demonstrates a commitment to beginning and/or continuing their personal learning journey related to Indigenous-specific racism and dismantling systems of oppression, as well as addressing racism more broadly. Shows willingness to articulate and share their learning experiences to contribute to a culture of motivation and inspiration among peers.
Demonstrates foundational knowledge of the social, economic, and political realities of settler-colonialism and its impacts on Indigenous peoples and equity-deserving groups within social and health contexts. Understands the impact of social determinants of health-on-health outcomes. Shows a commitment to learning about and upholding legislative obligations and provincial commitments outlined in foundational documents such as the Truth & Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action (2015), In Plain Sight (2020), BC's Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (2019), United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP), Reclaiming Power and Place: Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women & Girls Calls for Justice (2019), the Declaration Act Action Plan, Remembering Keegan: A First Nations Case Study, the BC Human Rights Code, Anti-Racism Data Act, and the Distinctions Based Approach.


What We Bring

Every PHSA employee enables the best possible patient care for our patients and their families. Whether you are providing direct care, conducting research, or making it possible for others to do their work, you impact the lives of British Columbians today and in the future. That’s why we’re focused on your care too – offering health, wellness, development programs to support you – at work and at home.


Join one of BC’s largest employers with province-wide programs, services and operations – offering vast opportunities for growth, development, and recognition programs that honour the commitment and contribution of all employees.
Access to professional development opportunities through our in-house training programs, including +2,000 courses, such as our San’yas Indigenous Cultural Safety Training course, or Core Linx for Leadership roles.
Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including municipal pension plan, and psychological health & safety programs and holistic wellness resources.
Annual statutory holidays (13) with generous vacation entitlement and accruement.
PHSA is a remote work friendly employer, welcoming flexible work options to support our people (eligibility may vary, depending on position).
Access to WorkPerks, a premium discount program offering a wide range of local and national discounts on electronics, entertainment, dining, travel, wellness, apparel, and more.

Salary Range: $76,111 - $109,409/year. The starting salary for this position would be determined with consideration of the successful candidate’s relevant education and experience, and would be in alignment with the provincial compensation reference plan. Salary will be prorated accordingly for part time roles.

Location: 1333 W Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6H 1G9

Closing date: Applications accepted until position is filled

Hours of Work: 08:00-16:30 (Monday to Friday)

Requisition #: 204059E

The Provincial Health Services Authority (PHSA) plans, manages and evaluates specialized health services with the BC health authorities to provide equitable and cost-effective health care for people throughout the province. Our values reflect our commitment to excellence and include: Respect people – Be compassionate – Dare to innovate – Cultivate partnerships – Serve with purpose.

Learn more about PHSA and our programs: jobs.phsa.ca/programs-and-services

PHSA is committed to equity in our hiring and employment practices. With learning and compassion, we are addressing existing inequities and barriers throughout our systems. PHSA is seeking to create a diverse workforce and to establish an inclusive and culturally safe environment. We invite applications and enquiries from all people, particularly those belonging to the historically, systemically, and/or persistently marginalized groups identified under the B.C. Human Rights Code.

One of PHSA’s North Star priorities is to eradicate Indigenous-specific racism, which includes dismantling barriers to health care employment at every level. We welcome Indigenous individuals to apply and/or contact the Sanya'kula Team (Indigenous Recruitment & Employee Experience) for support at indigenous.employment@phsa.ca.

Indigenous-specific anti-racism initiatives are rooted in addressing the unique forms of discrimination, historical and ongoing injustices, and marginalization faced by Indigenous peoples. You must apply via your internal profile at http://internaljobs.phsa.ca.

The internal job posting expires on September 21, 2026 and will no longer be accessible. Please do not apply for the external job posting.

If you have not yet set up an internal profile, please e-mail internaljobshelpu@phsa.ca with your PHSA employee ID number to obtain your temporary password. Clarity is redefining how private companies and their shareholders access liquidity. Through its institutional-grade platform, Clarity brings together buyers, sellers, and issuers to facilitate secondary transactions in venture-backed, pre-IPO companies, introducing efficiency, transparency, and standardization to an otherwise opaque asset class.

Recognized as one of Canada's fastest-growing companies and backed by leading U.S. investors, Clarity is profitable, well-capitalized, and building a high-performance team to meet growing demand and pursue new market opportunities.

Interested in learning more about life at Clarity? Check out our careers page to see how you can grow with us!

Are you the kind of person who's always raising your hand for the toughest challenge? Do you thrive in fast-paced environments, learn quickly, and want to build a career where finance meets technology?

We're looking for exceptional new graduates and early career professionals to join Clarity as a New Analyst in June 2027. This is an opportunity to accelerate your career by working alongside experienced operators, supporting high-impact initiatives, and gaining exposure to multiple areas of our business. You'll tackle meaningful work from day one, take ownership of real projects, and develop the analytical, operational, and client-facing skills that define top performers in financial services.

The strongest candidates won't just execute — they'll ask great questions, solve problems, and continuously look for ways to improve how we work. You will gain exposure to many aspects of the private securities industry.

Supporting live transactions and marketplace activity across Clarity's business.
Analyzing data, building reports, and generating insights that help drive business decisions.
Partnering with teams across Marketplace, Institutional Markets, Operations, and Client & Transaction Services to deliver exceptional client outcomes.
Maintaining accurate records and workflows using Salesforce and Clarity's internal systems.
Identifying opportunities to improve processes and help implement scalable solutions.
Working closely with experienced team members who will mentor and challenge you as you grow.
Taking on increasing ownership and responsibility as you demonstrate impact.

Recently completed (or are completing) an undergraduate degree in any discipline with an exceptional GPA (transcript required).
A proven track record of excellence, whether through academics, athletics, leadership, entrepreneurship, or extracurricular activities.
Internship, co-op, or work experience where you've demonstrated initiative, accountability, and strong execution.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in Excel.
Demonstrated experience using generative AI tools to solve complex problems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Curiosity, humility, and a desire to learn quickly in a high-performance environment.
Excited to work in person from Clarity's Vancouver headquarters.

Internship or coursework in finance, business, economics, engineering, or another quantitative field.
Experience using Salesforce or other CRM platforms.
Interest in private markets, venture capital, startups, or financial technology.

Title: Senior Research Analyst
Description:
Commercial Real Estate + Technology

Floorspace is a modern commercial real estate brokerage and technology company, building tools that make brokers faster, smarter, and more efficient. We pair a high-performing brokerage team with our proprietary platform, FLO, to redefine how deals get done.




We’re growing quickly—and we’re looking for a Senior Research Analyst who can level up our data, insights, and market intelligence.




About the Opportunity

As a Senior Research Analyst at Floorspace, you’ll be a core part of our research engine—responsible for leading our market data program, building high-quality insight products, and supporting brokers with the information they need to win business and advise clients.

This role goes beyond standard research: you’ll help shape how Floorspace collects, structures, and leverages data across Vancouver’s commercial real estate market. You’ll oversee data integrity across FLO, guide junior analysts, and collaborate closely with both our brokerage and product teams.




What You’ll Be Doing

Market Intelligence & Reporting

Lead quarterly and monthly market research for office, industrial, and retail sectors.
Produce data-driven reports, dashboards, and insights for clients, pitches, and internal visibility.
Monitor leasing activity, construction, subleases, and key market trends across Metro Vancouver.

Data Quality & System Ownership

Oversee and maintain the accuracy of core datasets within FLO (buildings, availabilities, leases, comps).
Establish and refine data standards for research across asset classes.
Improve research workflows and help drive automation and efficiency.

Business Development Support

Prepare insight packages for pitch decks and client proposals.
Identify opportunities in the market for tenant rep outreach, landlord listings, and strategic positioning.
Work closely with senior brokers to frame market narratives and support deal execution with data.

Leadership & Collaboration

Mentor and support junior analysts and interns.
Work cross-functionally with marketing to elevate our market storytelling.
Partner with our product and engineering teams to shape future FLO features that rely on research data.

Special Projects

Lead deep-dive studies (sublease trends, sector-specific analyses, demand patterns, etc.).
Contribute to new research formats such as our “Floorspace Five,” neighbourhood guides, and property analyses.




Who We’re Looking For

You’re not just comfortable with data-you know how to use it to tell a compelling story. You bring strong analytical grounding, an understanding of commercial real estate, and the ability to translate information into actionable insights.

You have:

3–5+ years of experience in commercial real estate research, valuation, data analytics, or a related field.
Strong knowledge of CRE fundamentals—leasing, market dynamics, submarkets, and asset types.
Advanced proficiency in Excel.
Experience managing datasets and ensuring data integrity.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, especially in synthesizing complex information.
Interest in working closely with both brokerage and product/tech teams.
A proactive, organized, and detail-oriented working style.




Why Join Floorspace?

A tech-enabled brokerage model:

You’ll work within a company where research actually matters - our proprietary tech (FLO) relies heavily on your work and insight.

A collaborative, entrepreneurial team:

Work directly with brokers, marketing, product managers, analysts, and leadership. Ideas are encouraged, and execution is fast.

High-impact role:

Your work will shape our market presence, influence client strategy, and power our internal platform.




Working Conditions

Our head office is located in downtown Vancouver. The team is primarily office-based, with some flexibility for hybrid work.




Compensation

Salary range: $70,000–$90,000, depending on experience.

Includes a performance-based bonus program.




Make an Impact

If you’re energized by data, passionate about real estate, and eager to play a meaningful role in the growth of a modern brokerage, we’d love to hear from you.




Floorspace values diversity and is committed to Employment Equity. Direct applicants only-no agencies. We thank all applicants for their interest; only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 

Learn more about us at www.floorspace.ca

Title: Coordinator, Quality Improvement & Analytics
Description:
Salary

The salary range for this position is CAD $38.88 - $55.89 / hour

Job Summary

Fraser Health is seeking a Full Time Quality Improvement and Analytics Coordinator to drive regional mobility, optimize multi-million dollar infrastructure, and pioneer sustainable transit solutions across British Columbia's premier healthcare networks. Use your education and business acumen in this vital operational role. Champion the day-to-day management of the Lower Mainland's consolidated parking portfolio, direct vendor contracts, optimize capital budgets, and lead facility design from blueprint to commissioning.

Detailed Overview

Supporting the Vision, Values, Purpose and Commitments of Fraser Health including service delivery that is centered around patients/clients/residents and families:

The Coordinator, Quality Improvement & Analytics, coordinates security incident reporting systems and data analytics programs for the Fraser Health Authority, Vancouver Coastal Health Authority, Provincial Health Services Authority and Providence Health Care (collectively, the "Organizations"). The Coordinator is responsible for the development, administration and management of the Business Intelligence tools and dashboards, IPS data warehouse and security incident reporting systems administration. Lead the design of methods and of tools in order to achieve consistent and reliable data collection. Responsible for the design and development of IPS data analytics reports for internal and external stakeholders. Leads the data quality control program, including the development of processes, end user education, and automated audits. Provides evidence to IPS senior leadership in support of both capital and operational budget requests. Leads the development and management of quality improvement and program evaluation initiatives within IPS.

Responsibilities


Leads and coordinates the collection, measurement and reporting of key performance indicators for the different IPS business streams. Collaborates with the IPS business streams to assess, plan and prepare statistical analysis for business cases and/or corporate service briefing notes. Coordinates and leads the development of site security statistical reports on quarterly bases, or as required, for dissemination to internal stakeholders.
Leads and coordinates quality assurance audits by reviewing audits for completeness, accuracy and integrity of security reports and aggregate data. Conducts regular audits to monitor business and operational processes and contract performance of contracted security provider. Analyses, compiles and reports on findings to IPS leadership teams, as required.
Responsible for providing data and security resourcing model design input for major projects across the Organizations.
Develops consolidated reports and dashboards (e.g. SSRS, SQL, etc.) that integrate information from a variety of Integrated Protection Services information systems. Summarizes information, provides trend analysis and prepares reports on summary of findings for various levels of stakeholder groups.
Leads and oversees the security incident reporting and data analytics systems. Ensures efficient and effective reporting of security data. Ensures the systems and reporting are in alignment with business processes.
Administers and manages the Business Intelligence tools and dashboards, IPS data warehouse, and security incident reporting systems by developing and designing methods and tools for consistent and reliable data collection. Manages the resources required to maintain those systems.
Reviews, develops and monitors contract and IPS operational staff training initiatives and curriculum for incident documentation. Actively monitors and evaluates staff performance to ensure adherence of data collection protocols. Recommends and implements appropriate staff training and/or orientation to ensure staff are knowledgeable and up to date with current IPS incident reporting process and procedures.
Provides expertise and advice in investigations involving staff related to matters of security or information technology. Plays a lead role in the application of security technology that may be required for sensitive investigations, including those with potential for employee disciplinary outcomes. Supports the development of action plans regarding issues including the investigation and determination of appropriate actions for the Organizations.
Participates in various meetings, committees and task forces to provide expertise and guidance on the reporting of violence prevention categories and other performance reporting related matters.
Leads and coordinates improvements to performance reporting through report automation, introduction of new tools and process improvement.
Leads and coordinates the implementation of quality improvement initiatives, including process mapping, review and testing of any system and application functionalities.
Collaborates with business units in identifying reporting needs, analyzing current procedures, reducing redundancies and ensuring reporting processes support business objectives. Develop statistical reports for various internal and designated external stakeholders to provide performance indicator data and related metrics for review and analysis.
Identifies and evaluates new initiatives, developments and trends in security and emergency management reporting through literature review, contact with peers at other organizations, industry advisory groups, professional associations and attendance at seminars, workshops and education programs. Communicates information and makes recommendations to appropriate IPS management designate. Facilitates the implementation of approved initiatives. Monitors initiatives and recommends and/or takes remedial action as directed.
Responsible for obtaining system and network accounts, and user access permissions for IPS systems.
Provides after hours on-call Manager function for IPS for the Organizations, as assigned.


Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor degree in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Information Technology, or a related field, supplemented with five (5) to seven (7) years' recent related experience in security or crime incident reporting systems and/or business analytics, including experience with Healthcare Security Operations, in a large complex organization; or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Designation as a Certified Health Care Protection Administrator (CHPA) would be an asset.

Competencies

Demonstrates the leadership practices of the Fraser Health Leadership Framework of Clear, Caring and Courageous and creates the conditions for people to succeed.

Professional/Technical Capabilities


Working knowledge of decision support solutions, information management, business processes, technologies and applications.
Ability to lead, plan, manage, organize, and problem solve.
Demonstrated ability to deal with others effectively.
Demonstrated ability to function effectively in a highly dynamic environment with changing priorities.
Working knowledge of LEAN and/or other related quality principles and their applications.
Ability to prioritize workload and meet deadlines.
Ability to develop and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as a member part of a team.
Ability to operate related equipment including applicable software applications.
Physical ability to perform the duties of the position.


About Fraser Health

Fraser Health is the heart of health care for over two million people in Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley in British Columbia, Canada, on the traditional, ancestral and unceded lands of the Coast Salish and Nlaka’pamux Nations and is home to 32 First Nations within the Fraser Salish region.

People - those we care for and those who care for them - are at the heart of everything we do. Our hospital and community-based services are delivered by a team of 50,000+ staff, medical staff and volunteers.

We are committed to planetary health and value diversity in the work force. We strive to maintain an environment of respect, caring and trust. Fraser Health’s hiring practices aspire to ensure all individuals are treated in an inclusive, equitable and culturally safe manner.

Together, we are the heart of health care.

Title: Data Scientist
Description:
🎨 OpusClip is the world's No.1 AI video agent, built for authenticity on social media.

We envision a world where everyone can authentically share their story through video, with no expertise needed. Within just 18 months of our launch, over 10 million creators and businesses have used OpusClip to enhance their social presence.

We have raised $50 million in total funding and are fortunate to have some of the most supportive investors, including SoftBank Vision Fund, DCM Ventures, Millennium New Horizons, Fellows Fund, AI Grant, Jason Lemkin (SaaStr), Samsung Next, GTMfund, Alumni Ventures, and many more.

Check out our latest coverage by Business Insider featuring our product and funding milestones, and our recognition as one of The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups in 2024.

Headquartered In Mountain View, We Are a Team Of 100 Passionate And Experienced AI Enthusiasts And Video Experts, Driven By Our Core Values


Be a Champion Team
Prioritize Ruthlessly
Ship fast, Quality Follows
Obsess over customers


Be a part of this exciting journey with us!

About The Role

OpusClip is looking for a product-oriented Data Scientist to help us build trusted metrics, improve data quality, and turn complex product and customer data into clear business decisions.

In this role, you will own critical definitions across feature adoption, weekly active usage, credit consumption, user segmentation, retention, and lifetime value. You will validate reporting data against its source, investigate data-quality issues, and lead analyses that help Product, Finance, and AI teams understand what is working, what is not, and where we should invest next.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable writing SQL, investigating unexpected data, defining metrics with stakeholders, and communicating a clear recommendation.

What You’ll Do

Strengthen data quality and metric governance


Validate reporting tables and dashboards against their source data.
Establish clear definitions, assumptions, sources, and owners for important metrics.
Develop monitoring for duplicate events, unexpected volume spikes, null values, stale data, and reporting discrepancies.
Investigate tracking and data-quality issues across product events and downstream reporting tables.
Help teams distinguish genuine changes in user behavior from instrumentation or pipeline problems.


Lead product and business analysis


Conduct post-launch analyses for major product features and workflows.
Analyze adoption, activation, funnels, retention, segmentation, and user behavior.
Translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical plans.
Turn findings into actionable recommendations for product and business stakeholders.
Support our data analyst with complex or high-priority analytical requests.


Support retention, LTV, and Finance analytics


Analyze subscriber retention, monetization, and customer lifetime value.
Compare user and revenue behavior across plans, segments, and payment platforms.
Partner with Finance to validate reporting logic and investigate discrepancies.
Communicate assumptions and data limitations clearly when working with financial and payment-related data.


Partner with our AI teams


Support data curation, measurement design, and evaluation for AI-powered product experiences.
Define offline and online success metrics for model-driven features.
Analyze model quality, user behavior, and post-launch business impact.
Partner on experimentation, segmentation, and ongoing performance monitoring.


What We’re Looking For


Typically 3+ years of experience in data science, product analytics, decision science, or a closely related field—or equivalent experience owning work at this level.

Title: Senior Analyst, Fulfillment Inventory Management
Description:
This is a high-impact role at the intersection of inventory, analytics, supply chain and strategy, with significant visibility across the organization. You will build models and turn complex data into actionable insights, identify risks and opportunities, and help drive meaningful business results.

The ideal person is a self-starter and strong program manager who can bring clarity to complex, cross-functional initiatives, build alignment across teams, and turn strategy into execution. A consulting background combined with strong retail or supply chain experience would be particularly relevant. There is also a strong continuous-improvement mandate - this is someone who will challenge how things are done and find better ways to drive results.

This is a contract through January 2028.




Who – The Company:

Our client is one of Vancouvers most sought-after companies to work for, with global operations and an impeccable reputation.




What- The Role:

The Fulfillment Inventory Management team plays a critical role in maintaining inventory health, optimizing network capacity, enabling strategic inventory placement across the NAM fulfillment network, and ensuring the timely exit of end‑of‑life inventory. They partner closely with a broad range of cross‑functional teams to deliver on investment commitments while governing the processes that support effective inventory management and end‑of‑life execution.

They design and evolve core operational processes, lead governance routines, strengthen organizational connectivity, and generate data‑driven insights that fuel continuous improvement and risk mitigation. Through consistent and scalable governance frameworks, we drive efficient, standardized inventory practices that improve product availability, maximize DC space utilization, and minimize impacts on DC operations.

This role will lead a team to deliver on key mandates and financial commitments in a highly cross-functional area.

Lead and influence cross‑functional forums (analyst through director level) to enhance collaboration and partnership in support of shared operational, financial, and strategic outcomes.
Build complex operational–financial models that quantify process impacts, identify key drivers and KPIs, evaluate scenarios, surface risks, and recommend actionable improvements.
Partner across the network to improve inventory health, accelerate end‑of‑life inventory turnover, and optimize DC space utilization and overall operational efficiency.
Drive cross‑functional KPI improvements (e.g. inventory health, capacity, labor efficiency) by leading root cause analysis, quantifying possible levers to improve, and enabling teams with the right data, tools, and governance routines to support strategic prioritization and accountable execution.
Analyze large, complex datasets (Excel, Power BI, and related tools) to generate timely, accurate insights to support operational and financial decisions.
Support a multi-million dollar savings portfolio by creating and enabling processes and tactical execution plans, leveraging strong cross-team communication and influencing skills to proactively identify risks and develop initial risk mitigation strategies.
Support existing processes and enable new optimizations by creating integrated tools that provide transparent KPI visibility and faster, more effective issue escalation and resolution.
Continuously optimize current-state fulfillment processes to improve accuracy, speed, and alignment with evolving business priorities and strategic direction.




Who- the Candidate:

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Supply chain or similar; Analytics is an asset; MBA or CPA preferred
5-8 years of experience, preferably in consulting, strategy or equivalent experience with product/supply chain internal function within a large corporation
4+ years of experience working within a highly cross-functional team
Proven ability to simultaneously manage multiple projects with varying timelines and scopes; including ability to plan, budget and manage project execution
Self-starter approach to work, with an eagerness to consistently meet and exceed objectives and foster this within your team
Excellent attention to detail given the complex nature of the work and the high exposure of the content across various groups and leadership
Creative thinking and excellent problem-solving skills – must be able to solve problems in a new way, seeing past what is established and create a new way of doing things
Demonstrated ability to create clarity and drive alignment towards a common goal and across team members in various functions
Advanced proficiency with MS PowerPoint, Excel, Word necessary. Experience using Power BI is an asset
Strong process documentation skills and excellent spoken and written communication skills (verbal and non-verbal)




How much:

Competitive hourly wage in the range of $55-57.50/hr + 4% vacation pay, if incorporated, please discuss with Swim.




Where:

Vancouver, hybrid working conditions, minimum 3 days onsite.




When & How To Apply:

Title: Fraud Prevention Analyst
Description:
About the Role

Punt is entering an exciting new phase of growth, with new products and verticals launching alongside our existing business. With that growth comes new revenue streams, new fund flows, new systems, and plenty of interesting finance problems to solve.




We are seeking a detail-oriented Fraud Prevention Analyst to join our Risk team, based on-site at our Vancouver head office. This role is critical to protecting our online platform from fraudulent activity, minimizing financial losses, and ensuring a safe experience for our customers. This position requires close collaboration with our Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative skills with 2–4 years of hands-on experience with fraud prevention, chargeback mitigation in electronic payments and data analysis.




What You'll Do

Monitor transactions in real time to identify, investigate, and mitigate fraudulent activity
Analyse chargeback and large datasets to detect emerging fraud patterns and trends
Develop, test, and refine fraud detection rules and models with moderate autonomy
Manage and resolve chargebacks, disputes, and payment reconciliation issues end-to-end
Collaborate closely with Customer Support, Product, and Engineering teams to improve fraud controls and customer experience
Prepare regular reports on fraud metrics, loss trends, and key risk indicators for leadership
Stay current on payment fraud trends, regulations, and industry best practices
Identify and help implement process improvements to reduce false positives and fraud losses
Mentor junior analysts or support onboarding as needed




What You Bring

Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field
Experience with fraud detection platforms or tools
2–4 years of experience working with electronic payments within North America, including chargeback processes and dispute resolution
Demonstrated experience analyzing and working with large datasets
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with moderate independence
Excellent attention to detail and sound judgment in ambiguous situations
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate data insights into actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Must be able to work on-site at our Vancouver office
Legally entitled to work in Canada




Nice to Have

Familiarity with machine learning concepts applied to fraud/risk modelling
Prior experience in e-commerce specifically
Hands on experience with SQL, Python, R, or similar tools

Title: Data Platform Analyst
Description:
Position Title: Data Platform Analyst

Position Status: Full-Time Regular

Department: Corporate Services

Employee Group: Teamsters Local 31

Location: 4515 Central Boulevard, Burnaby

Salary Range/ Wage Rate: PG T27 $3,734.48 - $4,413.08 bi-weekly




Our Corporate Services Department is seeking a Data Platform Analyst who will support and maintain enterprise data platforms, database systems, and analytics solutions. You will develop and optimize data pipelines, data models, and reporting solutions; administer and monitor database environments; troubleshoot operational issues; and liaise between client departments, technical staff, and vendors to keep data systems reliable, secure, and aligned to business needs.




You are a pragmatic, service-oriented data professional with strong technical depth across database administration, data engineering, and analytics, who can translate business requirements into well-governed, supportable data solutions and keep critical enterprise data platforms running dependably.




This role:

Installs and maintains database systems to ensure a high level of data availability; develops database architecture using established standards; maintains and ensures database and coding standards and quality assurance standards and procedures; assists with planning and coordinating data migration between systems; and assists with the development and maintenance of cloud database components.
Develops and maintains ETL (extract, transform, load) processes and data pipelines for data integration across platforms; designs and develops data models for data warehousing and business analytics; assists with data integration and transformation between data sources; supports data warehouse development and maintenance; and monitors and validates data flows to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Develops, implements and maintains data analytics solutions using enterprise business intelligence tools; works with business stakeholders to gather requirements, translate, and deliver data analytics solutions; creates and optimizes semantic data models, calculated measures, and data transformations for solutions; and provides training and assistance to business users on self-service analytic tools.
Monitors and evaluates technical performance of corporate data systems; identifies and resolves data abnormalities to avoid system outages; recommends replacement of aging systems and opportunities for optimization; assists with the monitoring and administration of cloud data storage solutions; provides technical support for operational issues; and participates in data backup and recovery planning.
Serves as a technical resource on various infrastructure and database projects; completes tasks according to project schedules; coordinates with departmental stakeholders to ensure that database standards remain relevant and aligned with business requirements; as required, oversees the work of consultants for compliance with corporate database and applications development standards.
Researches, evaluates and recommends information technology solutions and best practices related to data engineering, analytics, and data management; evaluates impacts of new technology and practices on existing systems; and prepares and presents related reports as required.
Maintains documentation for database configurations, data pipelines, reports and procedures.
Performs related work as required.




To be successful, you have:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, data engineering, business analytics or related discipline, plus considerable related experience in data analytics, data engineering and database administration; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
Considerable knowledge of relational database management systems, including the principles, methods, practices and procedures for database administration, maintenance, design and optimization.
Considerable knowledge of data engineering methods and procedures, including the tools and practices for extracting, transforming, loading data, automating and optimizing data pipelines for data integration.
Considerable knowledge of data analytic methods and procedures, including statistical analysis, data visualization and modeling techniques, processes and tools related to the work.
Considerable knowledge of the characteristics and capabilities of the District’s computing environment.
Considerable knowledge of problem definition and solution techniques applicable to the work.
Sound knowledge of the functions of departments served and their requirements as applied to the work.
Ability to analyze and evaluate various data and information requirements and to prepare data engineering and data analytics solutions to meet the needs of client departments.
Ability to develop databases including physical and logical data structures, using established standards.
Ability to evaluate and monitor the performance of databases and related applications to ensure data integrity, security and optimization of database resources, and to provide related technical support.
Ability to design and implement data transformation logic and pipeline workflows for data integration.
Ability to create and optimize data models, processes, queries, and calculated measures.
Ability to serve as a technical resource for enterprise infrastructure and database projects.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a variety of contacts, to communicate effectively, and to provide advice and assistance on matters related to the work.
Skill in using SQL, common programming languages, and enterprise business intelligence tools.
Driver’s Licence for the Province of British Columbia.

Title: Sales Operations Analyst
Description:
About Earthdaily

EarthDaily is revolutionizing the way we understand and monitor our planet. Through cutting-edge Earth Observation (EO) technology and geospatial analytics, we provide unparalleled insights for industries ranging from agriculture to mining, insurance, and government intelligence. Our mission is to build the world’s most advanced change detection system to capture, analyze, and interpret global shifts in near real-time.

OUR CREW

Our global, distributed team represents a variety of business lines and is made up of business development, sales, marketing and support professionals, data scientists, software engineers, project managers and finance, HR, and IT professionals. We are currently looking for a detail-oriented, Vancouver-based Sales Operations Analyst to join our crew!

READY TO LAUNCH?

Do you want to join one of the most exciting space companies at the forefront of global change detection/change monitoring? At EarthDaily, the Sales Operations Analyst is responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of our CRM and sales data across multiple lines of business and market verticals. This is a full-time, hybrid position based at our Vancouver Convention Centre office. Occasional travel may be required.

PREPARE FOR IMPACT!

As a Sales Operations Analyst, you will partner with the Sales Operations and Finance teams to identify, investigate, and resolve data quality issues, establish and enforce data entry standards, and maintain the governance processes that keep records consistent as the business scales.

As a detail-oriented problem solver with a systems mindset, you will leverage CRM tooling, reporting platforms, and all available processes to surface anomalies before they reach downstream reporting. You’ll take a proactive approach to data stewardship, routinely auditing records rather than waiting for errors to surface and translating recurring issues into durable process and system improvements. As a trusted resource to the sales and finance teams, you will ensure that account, opportunity, and pipeline data can be relied upon for forecasting, commission calculation, and executive decision-making.

Data Quality and Cleanup


Review and audit CRM records (contacts, accounts, opportunities, leads) for accuracy, completeness, and duplicates
Identify and correct data entry errors, missing fields, and inconsistent formatting in the CRM
Lead or support data cleanup projects such as deduplication, record merging, and standardizing naming conventions
Manage the import and validation of new leads or account data from third-party sources


Standards, Governance and Training


Establish and maintain data entry guidelines, and train and support sales reps on proper data entry practices
Maintain data definitions and a data dictionary for standard fields used across the sales team
Recommend process improvements to reduce recurring data quality issues
Escalate or collaborate with senior Sales Operations, Finance, and/or Data Governance staff on complex or cross-system data issues


Reporting and Metrics


Build and monitor data quality dashboards and reports, and investigate anomalies and trends
Track and report on data quality metrics (e.g., duplicate rate, field completeness, data decay) and remediation progress to Sales Operations and Finance leadership


Systems, Integrations and Automation


Partner with Sales Ops and IT on integration checks between the CRM and other connected sales tools (e.g., marketing automation, lead enrichment platforms)
Design and build sales automation and AI solutions to increase process efficiency and suggest improvements to the customer experience


YOUR PAST MISSIONS


Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, information systems, data analytics, data science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
1 to 4 years of experience in sales operations, sales support, data quality, revenue operations, or a related analytical role, with a proven track record of improving the accuracy and reliability of business-critical data
Hands-on experience administering or maintaining a CRM platform, including bulk data operations using data loaders, deduplication tools, or similar utilities
Demonstrated experience cleaning, reconciling, and manipulating large datasets (10,000+ rows) using advanced Excel functions such as INDEX/MATCH, nested IFs, array formulas, data tables, and Power Query
Experience building and maintaining dashboards and reports in a CRM or BI environment (Salesforce, HubSpot, Tableau, Power BI, or similar)
Exposure to data governance or data quality frameworks
Experience supporting forecasting, pipeline reporting, or commission processes in a SaaS or technical sales environment
Applied use of AI for analysis or automation


YOUR TOOLKIT


Deep working knowledge of CRM data structures, including the relationships between accounts, contacts, opportunities, and pipeline stages (HubSpot preferred but not required)
Understanding of sales and marketing processes and metrics (prospecting, lead gen, contracts, time to close, ACV/TCV/LCV, CAC/CPL, ROAS/ROMI, etc.)
Understanding of finance and reporting metrics (revenue recognition, backlog and pipeline calculations, close probabilities, growth scenarios, CAGR, etc.)
Has built, or can build, AI tools to automate sales processes (e.g., Claude, HubSpot Breeze)
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills, including VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, pivot tables, conditional formatting, and data validation
Basic to intermediate SQL for querying and validating data across systems
Strong attention to detail with a methodical, systematic approach to identifying, investigating, and resolving data issues
Understands the downstream impact of poor data quality on forecasting, reporting, and commission accuracy
Curious and inquisitive, excellent at asking questions to understand why an error occurred rather than only correcting it
Able to work independently on recurring data quality tasks while recognizing when to escalate; highly organized with excellent time management and the ability to balance competing priorities
Strong work ethic and self-drive, with an honest and ethical approach
Team player with a proactive and positive attitude, and experience collaborating with internal and cross-functional teams


Your Compensation

Base Salary Range: $55,000 to $80,000 CAD annually

The range is based on Vancouver, BC-derived compensation for this role. Individual placement in the range is determined based on many factors, including experience, skills, and qualifications. The top end of the range is typically reserved for individuals that meet or exceed all required qualifications and show demonstrated experience and expertise in all responsibilities of the role.

OUR SPACE

We’d love to welcome you to our world of software for space. We have a shared passion for building production critical systems that generate near real-time views of Earth from satellites that power real-world applications like disaster mitigation, environmental monitoring and crop yield improvements.

This is a full-time, in-office role at our Vancouver Convention Centre office, working in a fast-paced environment with regular collaboration across a team spread over North American time zones, and occasional travel (approximately 10%).

WHY EARTHDAILY ANALYTICS?


Competitive compensation, full benefits and flexible time off
Be part of a meaningful mission as part of one of Canada’s most innovative space companies that are developing sustainable solutions for our planet
Work from home opportunities (hybrid)
Great work environment, team and one of the best office locations in Vancouver (right over the water in the Vancouver Convention Centre)
Company subsidized lunches, lunch & learns and Friday afternoon social hours
