Title: Economics and Policy Analyst
Company: The Health Employers Association of BC (HEABC)
Description:
Are you looking to grow your career? Look no further than HEABC, the Health Employers Association of British Columbia. We contribute to the growth and sustainability of the BC health care system.

We Are Proud To Offer


In office or hybrid work environment – flexibility that suits your needs.
Competitive salary.
Four weeks of vacation, earned in your first year of employment & 13 statutory holidays.
Comprehensive health & dental benefits, with immediate coverage upon starting.
Pension Plan - BC’s Municipal Pension Plan is one of the largest pension plans in Canada and provides secure retirement income to plan members.
Training and development opportunities – HEABC supports your continuing education & growth.
A work environment which values work-life balance, respect, recognition, teamwork, and inclusivity.
The opportunity to make a positive contribution to the BC health care system through your work.


HEABC leads and supports the strategic planning related to human resources and labour relations on behalf of British Columbia’s publicly funded health employers. HEABC is responsible for negotiating provincial agreements for 190,000 unionized health care employees including nurses, physician residents, ambulance paramedics, health science professionals, and more.

HEABC Medical Staff Services leads a coordinated approach to the negotiation of provincial and local medical staff agreements and provides expert advice to health system partners on their relationships with medical staff. Join our highly talented team in a culture of learning, innovation, and visionary thinking. Join our highly talented team in a culture of learning, innovation, and visionary thinking.

The successful candidate may be permitted to work in a hybrid model (combination of in-office and flexible work location) and will live within commuting distance of our Vancouver office.

For more information, visit www.heabc.bc.ca

Opportunity

Reporting to the Director, Research and Analysis, the Economics and Policy Analyst (the Analyst) performs technical research work; carries out interpretive and analytical activities; engages in, and conducts complex costing work for, physician contract and Physician Main Agreement negotiations; provides economics assessments, evaluates and develops policy options related to the delivery of and compensation of physician services; prepares and presents reports, and provides advice to the Director to identify potential areas of research, objectives, methodologies and requirements.

This position requires initiative, creativity, critical thinking, attention to detail, quantitative skills, proficiency in analytical methods, and outstanding presentation and writing skills. In this role, you will partner with a wide range of system partners, including senior staff of the Ministry of Health, health authorities and other health system partners. The ideal candidate will have a passion for conducting research that supports evidence-based policy and the diplomacy to develop and maintain strong relationships.

Responsibilities Include


Fosters the development of partnerships between HEABC, health authorities, the Ministry of Health and other health system partners on projects related to the delivery of and compensation for medical services.
Co-develops materials (e.g. briefing notes and presentations) for and/or participates in the meeting program for the Provincial Medical Services Executive Council and other Ministry of Health/Health Authority committees where evidence and materials are required to support local or Provincial-level discussion, policy and decision-making.
Recommends the design of and carries out rigorous methodologies for literature reviews, environmental scans, quantitative and qualitative research.
Manages data collection and designs databases; works with very large data sets and multiple data sources – cleans, organizes, link, and structure data.
Develops, analyses, and interprets various statistical and economic data, research studies, wage and salary surveys, and policy options to support decision-makers with evidence-based, statistically supported, and methodologically consistent advice.
Prepares related presentations, data visualizations, studies, and/or reports that effectively communicate the results of research and analysis, to be used by HEABC and /or MOH.


Required Experience & Knowledge

A master’s degree in economics, statistics, mathematics, business, or a health or social science discipline and at least three (3) years of related research or policy experience, preferably in the health care sector;


Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint;
Experience with electronic research databases and analytical software; with proficiency in one or more of the following analytical tools: SAS, R, STATA, Tableau, SQL, or related.
Outstanding interpersonal, problem-solving, and written and verbal communication skills.


Salary Range: $90,770 to $119,135

Typical Hiring Range: $90,770 to $113,462

In determining salary, HEABC considers many factors including the successful candidate’s skillset and experience as well as internal equity. The final salary offer will be at HEABC’s sole discretion and presented as part of a competitive total compensation package.

How To Apply

If you’re looking for a fulfilling and challenging career within a dynamic organization, please submit a cover letter and resume outlining your experience at: https://healthemployersassociationofbc.bamboohr.com/jobs/

Title: Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist I (HPRS I)
Description:
Company Overview

Policy Reporter offers a suite of insights products and consulting services to enhance market access strategies and patient support initiatives. By tracking payer policies in near real time, we ensure that the largest pharmaceutical, medical device and diagnostics manufacturers, leading academic institutions and organized provider groups have the most up-to-date data and evidence-based guidance to help patients access the therapies they need. For more information, please visit https://www.policyreporter.com.

About The Team

Our Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist team is dedicated to delivering exceptional data quality, client satisfaction, and fostering strong team collaboration. We conduct in-depth research on the US healthcare landscape, helping clients analyze policy data that shapes their market access strategies. Through rigorous data synthesis and clear presentation of findings, we provide actionable insights that drive decision-making.

We're committed to comprehensive research, meticulous attention to detail, and solution-focused problem-solving. Our collaborative culture encourages open communication and mutual support as we navigate competing deadlines and complex deliverables. Beyond our work, we prioritize building genuine connections through monthly team lunches and virtual social activities, creating a welcoming environment where every team member can thrive.

Position Summary


The Healthcare Policy Reporting Specialist I, Research conducts in-depth research on US healthcare policy data and delivers comprehensive payer landscape projects that inform market access strategies for leading pharmaceutical, medical device, and diagnostics companies, as well as academic institutions and organized provider groups.
This role requires meticulous data extraction and analysis, exceptional attention to detail, and strong problem-solving abilities. You'll generate actionable insights from complex policy information while maintaining the highest standards of data accuracy.
Join a collaborative team that values work-life balance and offers flexible scheduling across time zones. As our team continues to grow, you'll have opportunities for professional development and career advancement.


Role & Responsibilities


Investigate and extract key healthcare payer policy data for client facing reports for both new and existing reports
Lead well-established reporting, ensuring continued high data accuracy and efficiency through thorough quality assurance of the policy data set across existing reports.
As required, HPRSs liaise directly with clients on projects to understand their needs, scope deliverables, and present findings.
Work collaboratively with internal stakeholders to conduct analysis and generate insights in the form of dashboards/visualizations for the clients.
With experience, HPRSs will take on additional responsibilities including but not limited to:
Provide support and guidance to new hires - participate in the mentorship program when requested and conduct training sessions.
As required, support cross-departmental strategic initiatives as a representative of the research team.
Evaluate current content & processes and develop innovative approaches for improvement to increase accuracy and efficiency
In line with ensuring the quality and accuracy of our reports, HPRSs will perform maintenance on a database of healthcare payer policies as needed
Perform maintenance of internal research tools
Conduct Quality Control checks on your own work, as well as the work of colleagues as required
Develop a deep understanding of the US healthcare landscape
Work independently with minimal supervision


Skills & Qualifications


Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel skills
Research competencies including but not limited to
Synthesizing and analyzing insights from large data sets
Summarizing, presenting, and defending findings to both internal and external stakeholders
Excellent organizational and problem-solving skills
High attention to detail
Effective verbal and written communication; ability to communicate and present findings to clients in a clear and concise manner
A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (life science, social science, language-focused humanities), or 1-3 years of experience in a similar role (data quality management or research) is considered an asset
Must have at least 1 year of Quantitative & Qualitative Research experience.
Experience and/or knowledge in Prior Authorization, Billing and Coding, and Medical reimbursement would be considered an asset
Experience in communicating findings to external clients is considered an asset
Prior knowledge of the US healthcare market is preferred
Previous healthcare data experience is considered an asset


General Pharmaceuticals:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in general pharmaceuticals including but not limited to neurosciences, cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, gastroenterology, infectious diseases areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.


Oncology/Immunology:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in oncology & immunology therapy areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical market access landscape is considered an asset.
A strong understanding of key concepts such as biomarkers, companion diagnostics, personalized medicine, biosimilars, cell & gene therapies, and monoclonal antibodies is preferred.


Medical Devices/Procedures:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in medical devices & procedures is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/medical device market access landscape is considered an asset.
Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes is considered an asset.
Expertise of medical device industry standards and compliance with launch and reimbursement experience is considered an asset.


Diagnostics:


In-depth scientific knowledge and/or previous work experience in diagnostic testing areas is preferable. Knowledge of the US pharmaceutical/diagnostic market access landscape is considered an asset.
Knowledge and/or experience in precision medicine and clinical genomics experience will be highly valued.
Knowledge and/or experience in working with Current Procedural Terminology (CPT)/Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Codes.
Experience in processing/approval of diagnostic coverage claims is considered as an asset


What We Offer


Competitive compensation package including extended health benefits, paid-time off, volunteer leave, employer-matching retirement savings, etc. and company paid Employee Assistance Program
Excellent opportunities for personal and career development
Collaborative and supportive company culture


Policy Reporter’s Core Values


Excellence
Value & Respect
Continuous Learning
Ownership & Accountability
Teamwork


Policy Reporter is committed to Employment Equity. Accommodations during the recruitment process are available upon request for candidates with disabilities.

  • Develop a deep understanding of the US healthcare landscape

Title: Member Contact Operations Analyst (12-Month Contract and 20-Month Contract)
Description:
Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.

As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,300 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!

Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As a Member Contact Operations Analyst, you will play a key role in enabling the development of optimized business results through data-driven insights. You will define and translate business needs into actionable requirements, develop operational reports using real-time and historical data, and collaborate with stakeholders to deliver solutions that enhance member experience. We’re looking for a detail-oriented, analytical thinker who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is passionate about leveraging technology to improve processes. Experience in Genesys Cloud admin will be integral for success in this role. 

This is a Full-time, Temporary role based at our Surrey Central Office or from your B.C based home office under remote working arrangements. While this position provides a hybrid work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.

How You’ll Make an Impact:

Defining, analyzing and interpreting business needs into clear business requirements, user stories, and process models
Developing cross-functional reports using data from multiple sources to meet business needs
Identifying process or access changes required and communicating these to stakeholders
Collaborating with end users to create new or enhance existing report templates in conjunction with IT teams
Contributing to project deliverables in both agile and waterfall methodologies
Supporting design, build, test, training, and deployment phases of projects
Creating and maintaining documentation for reporting processes and actively managed documents
Managing end-user profiles and permissions on Genesys reporting platforms
Support Genesys Cloud admin, with an emphasis on A3S, Snowflake, App Foundry, Kibana etc.


What You’ll Bring to the Team:

At least 2 years of post-secondary education in a relevant field (e.g Database Admin, Data Analytics, Data Science)
Minimum 2+ years of experience in a contact center environment
1+ year back-end administrative experience with Genesys Cloud Platform
Minimum 1+ year of experience with Database Management Systems (e.g., Power BI, SQL)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
Self-driven persistence in conducting deep data analysis to gain a comprehensive understanding, uncover insights, and resolve discrepancies.
Ability to communicate effectively and translate business requirements into technical specifications


Extra Skills That Set You Apart:

Experience providing technical guidance or acting as a subject matter expert
Familiarity with agile and waterfall project methodologies
Creativity in developing reporting solutions and improving processes


You’ll Thrive Here If You Are:

An Analyzer & Problem Solver - Skilled at detecting anomalies and resolving discrepancies.
Solutions-focused & Process-oriented - Confident in decision-making and improving tools and processes.
A Communicator with Influence - Able to present data effectively and collaborate with stakeholders.
Self-starter - Proactive and motivated to meet timelines and deliverables.


What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of $55,300 to $65,000 per annum. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:

Living Wage Employer: We’re the largest private-sector Living Wage Employer in Canada and consistently ranked among Canada’s Top Employers.
Customizable Benefits: Permanent employees receive flexible benefit packages that can be tailored annually to meet evolving needs.
Generous Vacation: New employees start with 3-4 weeks of vacation per year, with additional days earned over time.
Extra Stat Holidays: In addition to BC’s 11 statutory holidays, we offer 2 extra days, plus care days for personal or family illness.
Immediate Health Coverage: Health and dental benefits begin on your hire date, with three levels of coverage to choose from.
Defined Benefit Pension: Our retirement plan provides a guaranteed income for life, recognizing that retirement looks different for everyone.


Vancity Talent Programs:

Vancity supports an inclusive hiring process for candidates who self-identify as Indigenous, Black, or Trans. With special permission from the BC Human Rights Commissioner, this initiative provides access to career development opportunities, prioritized job screening, and feedback. Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). For details, please see our dedicated Talent Programs job posting.

At Vancity we’re committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace to help our people and communities thrive and prosper. Diversity in our workforce is integral so that we can truly represent, understand and respond to our community needs and deliver on our member experience.

We are also committed to an inclusive, barrier-free and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. If you require any accommodations or support at any stage of the recruitment process (including the application stage), we encourage you to let us know by contacting our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@vancity.com. We’re here to work with you to ensure your needs are met promptly and effectively. All requests will be handled with the utmost respect and confidentiality, so you can participate fully in the process.

Title: 26-61 Senior Business Intelligence Analyst (10 months)
Description:
The Opportunity

Supports the Leader in the strategy and operation of Technical Safety BC’s business intelligence program supporting driving operational efficiencies and measurement of organizational strategy implementation. Provides an advanced level of expertise in business intelligence to develop and deliver data and information products for internal and external customers and stakeholders. Independently carries out complex needs assessment, identifies opportunities to optimize use of data and information extracted from internal and external sources, and determines optimal methods to deliver resulting products to meet business needs. Provides day-to-day technical guidance to the Business Intelligence Analyst.

Status: Casual, Full-Time, Union

Number of Positions: 1

Pay Grade: (Grade 18) $61.87/hr

Location: Vancouver or open to any of our BC regional offices

Reports to: Leader, Business Intelligence

As a Senior Business Intelligence Analyst, you will:


Applies an advanced level of expertise in the strategy and operation of Technical Safety BC’s business intelligence program. Provides input to development of corporate strategies to influence change through data, information and knowledge, and participates in implementation and delivery.
Identifies information needs, including situations where clients cannot clearly articulate the need, available solutions fall short, and data is of lower quality. Designs, develops, and delivers complex data and information products that are scalable and accessible to internal and external customers through standard or unique reports and self-serve methods.
Leads and participates in data initiatives that are strictly speaking outside of Business Intelligence, including data definition, data modelling, data quality, information management, and records management.
Applies an advanced level of expertise in experimental design, applying creativity and exploring innovative solutions to address client-specific needs. Tests information products, evaluates findings, and redesigns as necessary to deliver required outcomes. Educates end users at senior levels of the organization on the proper use of BI products.
Supports the Leader in developing a framework of processes, practices and standards to ensure all product development and information sharing is executed with cost-effective, timely, and operationally efficient results. Develops ethical standards on the use of information within the organization. Fosters transparency and ready-access to information, while also establishing the necessary controls to mitigate risks.
Collaborates with the Information Technology and Data Management departments in identifying optimal solutions and delivering information services throughout the organization. Negotiates solutions and scheduling with IT/DM departments while maintaining excellent relationships with the IT/DM departments.
Collaborates with leaders to assess and advise on business intelligence needs, and determines optimal methods and products to support achievement of business objectives. Manages internal expectations and takes action to find common ground for differing agendas and conflicting objectives. Assesses and prioritizes day-to-day requests, applying judgement in the context of organization-wide requirements.
Collaborates with the Leader in providing communication and advice that encourages client behavioural change through use of data and information products. Appropriately addresses use of data and information that does not meet BCSA security, privacy, or ethical standards, with escalation to Leader or Director as necessary.
Supports the Leader in development of reports, presentations and business cases in support of business intelligence program initiatives.
Proactively resolves complex program issues and challenges (e.g. Operations), referring only the unresolved, escalated situations to the Leader for direction.
Conducts research and continuously maintains knowledge and awareness of the business intelligence practices, methods and related industry trends.
Provides day-to-day technical guidance to the Business Intelligence Analyst.



Knowledge, Skills & Experience you have:

Education And Experience

The required knowledge and skills for the position would typically be acquired through a Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or other related discipline and 6 - 8 years of experience in business intelligence in a measurement-intense environment, including experience working within IT teams in the delivery of BI solutions.

Achievement of (or eligible for) a relevant professional designation is also required.

Knowledge And Skills


Advanced practical knowledge of business intelligence concepts and solutions, use of external data, publishing open data, client-specific offerings, report and self-serve methods
Advanced ability to understand and transform user information needs into visually well-designed business intelligence products
Advanced understanding and application of experimental design, combined with creativity and curiosity to explore innovative solutions (evidenced by portfolio)
Advanced and diverse experience in implementing, deploying, and operating BI technology stacks.
Solid business acumen and ethics to assess business intelligence requirements and priorities in the context of differing agendas or conflicting objectives
Advanced understanding of IT systems, databases, and data management including data quality
Advanced communication and interpersonal skills to engage in collaborative dialogue with internal and external customers/stakeholders, establish common ground, and influence change
Solid planning skills to support the Leader in day-to-day operation of the business intelligence program.
Advanced analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills to identify and take action to assess needs, address challenges, and manage change
Basic leadership skills to provide day-to-day technical guidance



Beyond the role:


Community & Wellness – We recognize and respect each other’s diverse needs. We strive to maintain a healthy culture of psychological safety, belonging, and space to prioritize healthy minds and well-being. This includes Wellness Wednesday (meeting free time), flexible paid holidays, a free subscription to the Calm app, and a flexible hybrid work environment focused on connections. Our teams also enjoy giving back to the community, and having fun, whether volunteering in the community, or running together on our Sun Run team. In 2023, Technical Safety BC donated to Crisis Centre BC, Aboriginal Coalition to End Homelessness, BC Wildfire Recovery, PADS, and Rise to Thrive Foundation.
Employee Resource Groups – We have Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) for Mental Health & Wellness, Indigenous Relations & Reconciliation, and Equity Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) to support initiatives we’re passionate about.
Learning & Development – We value giving and receiving feedback, as well as encouraging different ways for us to continuously learn as a company. This can be through lessons learned, wrap up sessions, one-on-one meetings, and team or individual courses, workshops, and conferences. In addition, we offer up to $1500 tuition aid per calendar year to support your education and learning goals.
Compensation & Benefits – In full transparency, you can find our industry-competitive compensation information on our postings. For our regular employees, we have outstanding benefits that include extended health, dental and disability coverage, access to an employee and family assistance program (EFAP), competitive annual paid vacation entitlements, public service defined benefit pension plan, generous top-up allowance for new parents, and time-off for caregiving, moving, and adoption leave. We recently upgraded our mental health benefits to $1500 separate from our non-mental health paramedical services too.



About Technical Safety BC

At Technical Safety BC, we matter to each other. Together, we apply a systems mindset to safety, embrace possibility, and act on what we learn. Our culture empowers and enables innovation and connection. Our environment welcomes diverse perspectives and learning is celebrated. We make decisions based on data and use our expertise to make the safety system equitable for all. 

Our values guide our work.


We see genius in diversity
We foster confidence
We make the complex simple
We adapt



Technical Safety BC is an independent, self-funded organization that oversees the safe installation and operation of technical systems and equipment across the province. In addition to issuing permits, licenses and certificates, we work with industry to reduce safety risks through assessment, education and outreach, enforcement, and research. Through simplification of our initiatives, we promote understanding and engagement, making safety accessible to everyone. As society changes, we create and adopt new ideas, skills, and tools that will enable us to meet the safety challenges of a highly-connected world.

We see genius in diversity and are committed to creating an equitable and inclusive workforce. We recognize that diverse life paths and experiences contribute to the overall qualifications for each role. If you feel that you could excel in this position, but do not necessarily meet the formal requirements, we encourage you to apply.

If you are interested in one of our career opportunities and require accommodation or assistance with the application or recruitment process, please contact us directly at careers@technicalsafetybc.ca.

If you are interested in this position, please apply online by 4:00pm PT on October 2nd, 2026. This opportunity will remain posted until filled; however, priority consideration will be given to those who apply by the deadline. To see a full list of our current opportunities or to learn more about working at Technical Safety BC, please visit our careers page.

Title: Analyst/Administrative Assistant
Description:
Come work as an Analyst/Administrative Assistant with Vancouver Coastal Health (VCH) on the Richmond Community Administration team. Apply now to join the team!

As an Analyst/Administrative Assistant with Vancouver Coastal Health you will:


Provide analytical support to the Program team for purposes such as data analysis, statistical reporting, benchmarking activities, developing and generating queries, preparing and compiling reports and technical documents utilizing various software and tools.
Provide confidential administrative and secretarial assistance and research support to the Director and to the IWMS team.
Maintain the Manager and management team’s appointment calendars, coordinate meetings, process and prioritize information, screen, triage and act upon requests and inquiries, including confidential and sensitive information.
Work independently and interface with other Executive Directors, Managers and staff at all levels of the organization.
Effectively partner with other VCH departments and liaises on behalf of the department with external agencies to coordinate the flow of information, keeping the Director apprised of relevant issues and activities.


This work is framed within VCH’s commitments to our pillars of Indigenous Cultural Safety, Anti-Racism, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, and Planetary Health.

Title: Senior Business Solutions Analyst
Description:
Union/Affiliation: Administrative and Professional Staff (APSA)
Pay range: $92,654 to $110,544 annually
SFU Department Descr: School of Medicine - Operations
Position Grade: 11
# of openings: 1
Biweekly Hours: 72





Who We Are

Help build B.C.’s new medical school from the ground up!

At the SFU Medical School, we envision a medical education system where students and residents learn as part of a team in primary care and other community-level settings, in patient-centered environments, and with a curriculum that considers social, environmental and prevention contexts. As we establish the school in Surrey, B.C., our growing relationships with the local community, Fraser Health Authority, First Nations Health Authority, physicians and Indigenous partners will help us to meet the diverse health needs of the communities we serve and improve access to primary care throughout the province. We seek to advance reconciliation by embedding and equalizing Indigenous knowledge systems in our learning, research and practices while resting on a solid foundation of high-quality, accredited education and world-class research efforts that keep us oriented toward measurable, socially accountable outcomes.





About The Role

The Senior Business Solutions Analyst will help shape the systems, processes and data infrastructure that support the continued growth of SFU’s Stephens Family School of Medicine. This role will translate complex business and operational needs into practical, scalable solutions that improve efficiency, strengthen decision-making and enhance the delivery of medical education programs and services. Working closely with senior leaders, faculty, staff, learners and technology partners, the role will lead initiatives spanning business analysis, workflow redesign, process automation, system implementation, data analytics, reporting and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to build innovative digital solutions using tools such as Power Apps, Power Automate, SharePoint and Microsoft Lists, while developing dashboards, KPIs and decision-support products for leadership. As the School continues to evolve, this role will contribute to new system implementations, operational modernization, reporting and governance frameworks, and large-scale transformation initiatives—helping establish sustainable infrastructure for the school’s future.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, analytical and solutions-oriented professional who can translate complex business needs into effective systems, processes and actionable insights. They bring strong experience in business analysis, process and workflow optimization, data analytics, business intelligence, reporting and automation, with the ability to design scalable digital solutions using tools such as Power Apps, Power Automate, SharePoint and Microsoft Lists. Strong project management, facilitation, stakeholder engagement and change management skills are essential. The successful candidate is a critical thinker with sound judgment, strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate complex information clearly to diverse audiences. Experience in healthcare or post-secondary environments, data governance, Indigenous data sovereignty and culturally safe practices would be an asset.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business administration and five years of related experience, including operational management, strategic planning, project management, personnel management or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.


Business Analysis & Solution Design – Ability to translate complex business requirements into scalable systems, workflows and effective digital solutions.
Data Analytics & Reporting – Strong expertise in data analysis, KPI development, business intelligence, dashboards and decision-support reporting.
Process Automation & Technology – Experience designing automated workflows and digital solutions using tools such as Power Apps, Power Automate, SharePoint and Microsoft Lists.
Project & Change Management – Ability to lead complex initiatives, facilitate cross-functional collaboration and support organizational change and process modernization.
Strategic Thinking & Stakeholder Engagement – Strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders and provide clear, actionable recommendations.


What We Offer

At SFU, our goal is to ensure our people are valued and supported by promoting a healthy work-life balance, professional growth and development, as well as a safe and respectful workplace. We offer temporary employees who belong in the Administrative & Professional Staff Association (APSA):


An additional 7% pay in lieu of benefits & 8% vacation pay
Employer paid extended health & dental plans
Professional development funds (minimum contract period of 1 year)
Hybrid-work program for eligible positions
Prorated for part-time employees


Additional Information

The assignment end date is August 27, 2027.

Please include your cover letter and resume in one attachment.

SFU is an equity employer and strongly encourages applications from all qualified individuals including women, Indigenous Peoples, visible minorities, people of all sexual orientations and gender identities, persons with disabilities, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of the university.

We are committed to ensuring that the application and interview process is accessible to all applicants. If you require any assistance or accommodations, please contact pei_reception@sfu.ca.

Analyze market trends, consumer behavior, and competitive activity.


Identify opportunities for growth, innovation, pricing, and assortment improvements.


Develop category strategies that support business objectives.



Support Retail Partners



Deliver category reviews, insights, and recommendations to retail customers.

Recommend assortment, promotion, and merchandising opportunities.

Create dashboards, reports, and performance reviews.

Eligible to work full-time in Canada.

Title: GIS Analyst
HTML:
Explore A Career At Mosaic
Mosaic is a diversified, 100% Canadian-owned land solutions company focused on long-term value creation from private forest lands and public forest tenures. Through an integrated, multi-use approach, Mosaic manages its land base across sustainable forestry, renewable energy, watershed services, recreation, real estate and carbon programs, bringing together innovation and stewardship to strengthen economic performance and environmental resilience. By aligning these complementary uses within a single land portfolio, Mosaic builds lasting value while helping shape the future of sustainable land management. Learn more at MosaicForests.com.

The Opportunity 
Mosaic is seeking a GIS Analyst to work out of one of our Vancouver Island offices in Nanaimo, Nanoose Bay, or Campbell River, British Columbia.

The Role 
Reporting to the Manager, Forest Information Systems (FIS) Services, the GIS Analyst takes on the full range of spatial work across Mosaic’s landbase, from sustainable forestry and watershed services to renewable energy, recreation, real estate and carbon projects. One week might involve improving inherited data and rebuilding a workflow; the next, running an analysis for an operational plan and producing a map series for field crews, or scoping spatial data for a new project. We're looking for someone comfortable taking on an unfamiliar problem and working out how to solve it. Specific responsibilities will vary with business priorities and and will include:

  • Conduct spatial analyses that support operational planning and land management decisions — constraint and net-area analysis, terrain modelling, suitability assessment, and change detection;
  • Integrate and quality-control spatial data from internal, contractor, provincial, and third-party sources — layouts, as-builts, cruise data, imagery and LiDAR;
  • Produce operational maps, map series, and web maps for field crews, reports, and regulatory submissions;
  • Automate repetitive analysis and data workflows using Python, ModelBuilder, and FME; and
  • Work directly with planners, foresters, and project teams to scope spatial data needs and translate results into clear, actionable insights.

What We’re Seeking:

  • Post-secondary degree or diploma in GIS, Geography, Geomatics, Forestry, Environmental Science, or a related spatial discipline;
  • Minimum of 3+ years of experience in GIS analysis, spatial data management, and cartographic production;
  • Solid spatial data QC skills — the ability to find and fix problems in data from a range of sources;
  • Strong working knowledge of the Esri ArcGIS Suite, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and ArcGIS Enterprise;
  • Experience building and maintaining project and file geodatabases, and working within established data standards;
  • Experience automating GIS processes using Python, ModelBuilder, and/or FME;
  • Working knowledge of relational databases, including MS SQL Server, in a GIS environment;
  • Comfort working across a variety of project types, including unfamiliar ones, with limited direction;
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills;
  • Ability to collaborate effectively, communicate clearly, and manage multiple priorities;
  • Familiarity with Trimble Land Resource Manager (LRM), forestry data systems, and coastal BC terrain is considered an asset; and
  • Forestry work experience and/or registration with the ABCFP as an RPF or RFT (or eligibility for registration) is considered an asset.

Mosaic values diversity and recognizes that talent comes in many forms. Even if you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re eager to learn about your unique knowledge, skills and experiences. 

What You Get
We are proud of our highly collaborative, respectful, and innovative work environment. Our employees are empowered with high levels of role autonomy and the ability to make decisions and lead change.

At Mosaic, we believe in rewarding our employees with a comprehensive and competitive package that reflects the value they bring to our team. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect when you join us:

  • Competitive compensation that matches your skills and experience.
  • Annual bonus tied to both individual and company performance, recognizing your contributions to our success.
  • Employer-paid premiums for a robust benefits package to support your wellness.

Job Summary

The Department of Psychiatry at the University of British Columbia invites applications for a full-time Research Computing Analyst with expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning and scientific computing. The successful candidate will work under the direct supervision of the Principal Investigator, Prof. Sophia Frangou, President’s Chair in Brain Health, and will receive detailed instructions on assignments. The successful candidate will carry out programming and technical tasks, troubleshoot computational problems, and contribute to the development and implementation of solutions under the guidance of senior members of the research team. Work will be reviewed for accuracy, completeness and timeliness.

The successful applicant will primarily contribute to the CentileBrain Project. This is a computational neuroimaging initiative focused on individual-level brain characterization. It combines large-scale imaging data, normative modelling, harmonization and machine learning. The platform generates individualized centile and deviation scores across the lifespan. The goal is to support precision neuroscience and clinically meaningful individual inference.

The Department of Psychiatry at the University of British Columbia invites applications for a full-time Research Computing Analyst with expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning and scientific computing. The successful candidate will work under the direct supervision of the Principal Investigator, Prof. Sophia Frangou, President’s Chair in Brain Health, and will receive detailed instructions on assignments. The successful candidate will carry out programming and technical tasks, troubleshoot computational problems, and contribute to the development and implementation of solutions under the guidance of senior members of the research team. Work will be reviewed for accuracy, completeness and timeliness

Work Performed


Oversees the implementation of established machine-learning, artificial-intelligence and statistical methods in research datasets, modifies existing scripts as required using detailed specifications, and recommends computational workflow modifications to the PI.
Performs data preparation, quality control, feature extraction and other defined computational tasks for large-scale research studies.
Integrates multimodal datasets using established analytical procedures and modifies existing code as required to support data compatibility and processing.
Runs and maintains computational workflows on local and high-performance computing systems, including monitoring processing and addressing routine execution issues.
Resolve routine technical problems in code, data processing and computational workflows and escalate new issues for consultation with senior team members.
Provides first-level technical support to research team members using established computational workflows and systems.
Maintains clear documentation of code and script modifications, analytical procedures, software versions, testing results and computational outputs.


Consequence of Error/Judgement

The Principal Investigator will provide oversight for this position. Given the importance of the work to the research program, errors or poor judgment could substantially compromise research quality, delay project completion, and adversely affect future funding opportunities. Inaccurate or ineffective representation of the team’s work could also damage relationships with funding agencies and collaborators. The position therefore requires consistently high standards of accuracy, judgment, efficiency, and communication.

Supervision Received

The successful candidate will work within the broad direction established by the Principal Investigator and research team, with a high degree of independence and minimal supervision. The successful candidate will be expected to exercise sound judgment in carrying out defined responsibilities, collaborate effectively with team members, and proactively identify and bring emerging issues, risks, or unusual circumstances to the attention of the Principal Investigator.

Supervision Given

The successful candidate may assign tasks to students and provide oversight and review of their work.

Minimum Qualifications

Undergraduate degree in a relevant discipline. Minimum of one year of related experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.


Willingness to respect diverse perspectives, including perspectives in conflict with one’s own
Demonstrates a commitment to enhancing one’s own awareness, knowledge, and skills related to equity, diversity, and inclusion


Preferred Qualifications


An undergraduate or master’s degree in computer science, data science, artificial intelligence, bioinformatics, computational biology, biomedical engineering, statistics or a related quantitative discipline.
Experience with analyses of human neuroimaging MRI data
Strong programming skills
Demonstrated experience in machine learning, artificial intelligence or advanced statistical modelling.
Experience working with high-dimensional or complex biomedical, biological or scientific datasets.
Effective written and oral communication skills.
Note: Candidates are not expected to have expertise in all of these areas. We are particularly interested in applicants who combine strong computational skills with the ability and interest to apply them to human neuroscience and biomedical research

Title: Sr Product Data Scientist
Description:
Your work days are brighter here.

We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

About The Team

Workday stands at a pivotal point in its evolution and growth. As we accelerate our Enterprise AI Transformation we must focus with equal intensity on scaling our execution to enable a rapid speed of continuous innovation for our customers. The Product & Technology (P&T) Operations Analytics & Tools Team develops decision-ready internal products that turn complex organizational data into targeted leadership action. Our vision is to: Power the strategic intelligence that scales how P&T operates with alignment and speed.

About The Role

We're looking for a business, product, and customer-oriented Senior Product Data Scientist to be the analytics partner for the Workday Data Cloud business. This role requires focused passion and excitement unlocking data insights that directly tie to strategic execution.

This role sits at the intersection of Workday's Data Cloud business, partnering directly with the Data Cloud organization (SVP/GM, Product Management, Engineering, and GTM teams) to bring analytical rigor and powerful business insights to a fast-growing, consumption-based product line. You will be the investigatory lead on a number of broad business questions. You will dive into the raw business data, find the root cause, and deliver an opinionated, decision-ready conclusion, not just more data.

You'll need to become a genuine subject-matter expert in Workday Data Cloud's business data landscape, working closely with the Workday Data Cloud GM and Product Management team. Your findings, and the curated data and documentation you produce along the way, should compound: feeding a shared knowledge base that makes the next question easier to answer, for you and for AI-assisted tooling built on top of the same body of work.

Key Responsibilities


Serve as the business analytics domain expert for Workday Data Cloud, providing technical and strategic thought leadership.
Partner cross-functionally across Go-To-Market (GTM) and Product teams to develop end-to-end views of the business, connecting the dots between top-of-funnel demand growth, sales pipeline, and downstream product usage.
Translate complex data models into compelling narratives and stories (including interactive visualizations and executive presentations) that drive organizational clarity.
Operate directly with SVP/GM-level stakeholders, translating a stream of layered, high-velocity questions into structured analysis without needing fully scoped requirements up front.
Translate ambiguous business, data, and platform questions into simple and focused conclusions, independently and with strategic judgment
Support consumption-based pricing and impact analysis for Workday Data Cloud, including sensitivity analysis, exploring new business models and driving business growth
Navigate real data-maturity and instrumentation gaps with autonomy: identifying what already exists, what must be built, and when to escalate.
Contribute well-documented, curated data assets and context back into the shared knowledge base so that analysis compounds over time and can eventually be self-served.
Design and influence Workday Data Cloud internal business data connections, collaborating with Product Management and engineering teams on the design, scalability, and sustainability of associated pipelines.
Leverage strong data ETL and data processing expertise to manage multi-step flows across product telemetry and observability systems
Demonstrate urgency and autonomy in problem-solving, proactively navigating cross-functional teams to identify and implement solutions for both known and emerging business challenges.


About You

You possess a deep interest in grasping the complex challenges that businesses face, and you are excited by solving problems. You have strong business acumen and are outcomes focused. Learning new tools and technologies motivates you. You embody the qualities of an insightful, thoughtful, and reliable teammate - and you expect the same of your teammates. You thrive in a fast-paced, tech start-up like environment where the best ideas win. “Think Like a Scientist” is ingrained in how you work - always hypothesizing, always experimenting, always learning.

You're energized, not intimidated, by building trust, process, and domain expertise in a new, growing business space. You default to curating and documenting what you learn, because you know the same data landscape will get harder questions tomorrow. You're comfortable moving between hands-on data work and strategic, executive-level framing.

Basic Qualifications


8+ years of experience with advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and/or data science
8+ years experience simplifying complex technical concepts for diverse stakeholders.
6-8 years experience working autonomously in a highly matrixed, collaborative corporate environment.
5+ years experience in business/product analytics, applied data science, or a related quantitative role, ideally supporting a product or platform organization.
5+ years experience in enterprise BI platforms (e.g.,Tableau, Sigma)


Other Qualifications:


Strong SQL and data-modeling skills; comfortable working directly in raw, partially documented, or partially instrumented datasets.
Familiarity with front-end components or frameworks (e.g., React, Node.js, JavaScript) to help collaborate with engineering peers.
Working familiarity with cloud data pipelines/ETL concepts (e.g., Airflow) sufficient to partner effectively with data engineering and platform product management teams.
Experience with SaaS pricing analytics or usage-based/consumption pricing models specifically.
Strong project management skills
Experience applying organizational change management principles
Experience working within an Agile/Scrum framework.
Experience within the SaaS, cloud, or enterprise technology industries
Strong communication and data storytelling skills
Demonstrated experience designing, developing, and maintaining enterprise production-level data science-based products for business decision-making
Experience on AWS stack (Redshift, Sagemaker), scripting languages (Python and R)
Degree in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Operations Research, Economics, or a related field) or equivalent practical experience.
Understanding of product management fundamentals

Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

Title: Analyste de l’information
Description:
La personne titulaire est chargée de mener des enquêtes fondées sur le renseignement de sources ouvertes afin d’appuyer les activités de la Mise en application de l’OCRI. Son rôle ne se limite pas à la collecte de données : il consiste également à interpréter et à synthétiser des renseignements complexes provenant de diverses sources, à dégager des tendances, des liens et des constatations clés qui orientent la stratégie relative aux dossiers et ouvrent de nouvelles pistes d’enquête. La personne titulaire transforme des données brutes et des éléments de preuve en renseignement clair donnant matière à intervention disciplinaire. En collaboration avec les équipes de la Mise en application, elle joue un rôle essentiel dans l’avancement des enquêtes par l’exercice de son jugement analytique, le maintien de l’intégrité des données et la gestion de multiples priorités dans un environnement dynamique axé sur les dossiers.

Principales responsabilités

Enquêtes


Mener des enquêtes approfondies sur les sociétés autorisées et les personnes autorisées en réponse aux plaintes du public (dont celles traitées par l’Évaluation des dossiers de l’OCRI), en réalisant des recherches exhaustives à partir du renseignement de sources ouvertes.
Consulter des bases de données internes et externes, des sources ouvertes et les médias sociaux afin de recueillir, de valider et d’analyser le renseignement pertinent.


Analyse et soutien à la Mise en application


Collaborer avec les équipes de la Mise en application en organisant, en interprétant et en présentant des données et des éléments de preuve à l’appui des dossiers en cours, y compris en préparant des pièces matérielles et en présentant les constatations à la direction et aux collègues.

Title: EA Sports FC Player Experience Analyst - FC Quality Verification
Description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

FC Live Platform Quality Verification is searching for the next game product expert to drive critical activities that support creating an optimal player experience and will be a key point of contact for decision-making from our stakeholders across production and development teams. The EA Sports FC Player Experience Analyst will report to the Development Manager.

Responsibilities


Create data-driven insights, reports and presentations to showcase trends and players' sentiment
Help promote game and experiential quality across FC by applying “the voice of the player"
Be an advocate of “the voice of the player” by creating a bridge between FC Live Platform Quality Verification and our partners
Promote improvements across functional quality; with a main focus on experiential quality
Monitor internal communication channels, public discussion forums, and social media platforms to help identify player-affecting issues and collect players' feedback
Coordinate with Production to prioritize recurring player feedback effectively


Qualifications


Bachelor's degree or equivalent industry experience in Quality Assurance
4+ years of experience with testing and defect tracking software, preferably Jira
4+ years of experience with Agile/Scrum software development methodologies
Synthesize community feedback and player sentiment into clear, relevant insights that can be discussed with producers and Live Operations partners to improve the player experience
2+ years of experience writing reports and providing updates to stakeholders
Knowledge of gaming consoles and their systems
Experience using collaboration tools, preferably Confluence, Miro, and Slack
Experience working across different time zones and international teams
Understanding of football tactics and in-game strategies.
A genuine love for football as a fan, player, referee, gamer, or coach.
Please include a cover letter to let us know your love/knowledge of the FC game or football (soccer) as a sport.


Learn more about QD from some of our team members at Electronic Arts: Ravi Minhas | Jessica Myk | Rob Weber | Barbara Homewood

Pay Transparency - North America

Compensation And Benefits

The ranges listed below are what EA in good faith expects to pay applicants for this role in these locations at the time of this posting. If you reside in a different location, a recruiter will advise on the applicable range and benefits. Pay offered will be determined based on a number of relevant business and candidate factors (e.g. education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, or business needs).

PAY RANGES


British Columbia (depending on location e.g. Vancouver vs. Victoria) *$77,700 - $107,900 CAD


Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA.

For Canada, we offer a package of benefits including vacation (3 weeks per year to start), 10 days per year of sick time, paid top-up to EI/QPIP benefits up to 100% of base salary when you welcome a new child (12 weeks for maternity, and 4 weeks for parental/adoption leave), extended health/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, disability insurance, retirement plan to regular full-time employees. Certain roles may also be eligible for bonus and other incentive programs.

About Electronic Arts

We’re proud to have an extensive portfolio of games and experiences, locations around the world, and opportunities across EA. We value adaptability, resilience, creativity, and curiosity. From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

We adopt a holistic approach to our benefits programs, emphasizing physical, emotional, financial, career, and community wellness to support a balanced life. Our packages are tailored to meet local needs and may include healthcare coverage, mental well-being support, retirement savings, paid time off, family leaves, complimentary games, and more. We nurture environments where our teams can always bring their best to what they do.

Electronic Arts is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, religion, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, marital status, family status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We will also consider employment qualified applicants with criminal records in accordance with applicable law. Title: Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data
Company: BC College of Nurses and Midwives
Description:
Status: Regular, Full-Time

Work Location: Hybrid, Vancouver B.C. (a minimum of 2 days in office)

Who We Are

The British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (“BCCNM”) is the college empowered under the Health Professions and Occupations Act to regulate the practice of all licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, registered midwives, registered nurses, and registered psychiatric nurses in British Columbia. Regulation helps to protect the public by ensuring that professional care or service received by the public is competent, ethical, and meets the standards that society views as acceptable.

As western Canada’s largest health profession regulator, we believe a diverse and inclusive team enriches our efforts to protect the public. We welcome applications from all who reflect of the communities we serve and especially encourage Indigenous Peoples and members of equity-seeking groups to apply. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences bring both innovation and better outcomes to the work we do and the decisions we make.

BCCNM’s commitment to Indigenous Specific Anti-Racism

BCCNM is committed to working with Indigenous Peoples and health system partners to support Indigenous-specific anti-racist practices in the health system. As the largest health regulator in Western Canada, BCCNM has the opportunity to influence the health professionals we regulate, as well as the broader health-care system, to break the cycle of racism, and improve health outcomes for Indigenous Peoples. BCCNM has pledged to become culturally safe and anti-racist, and to support the health professionals we regulate to do the same.

What We Offer You

We are delighted to be recognized as one of BC’s Top Employers. It is more than a badge of honor – it’s a reflection of our people and the purpose that drives us every day. At BCCNM, we’re creating a workplace where flexibility, equity, growth, and connection are not just values – they’re part of how we work. Whether it’s through hybrid work options, meaningful employee engagement, or our commitment to reconciliation, we’re building something that matters. This honor reflects our unwavering commitment to creating a workplace where people truly thrive.

We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

The expected starting base salary for this position is $111,320 – $116,886 annually, depending on a variety of factors including qualifications and experience. Once hired, you will progress through a wider salary range over time as you continue to develop job knowledge, skills and competencies for the role.

In addition to base salary, the college offers a generous vacation and extended benefits package. As an employee, you receive 100% employer-paid health and dental benefits. And we contribute to B.C.'s Municipal Pension Plan to help you secure your retirement income. Throughout your career with us, you will engage in a variety of learning and development. We will support your professional development and cover your professional membership costs. To support you in work and life, we provide an employee assistance program and fitness allowance perk. Working with us allows you to enjoy flexible hybrid work. This position is located in Vancouver, but you’ll be able to work remotely up to 3 days a week. What You’ll Be Doing

The Senior Analyst, Regulatory Data plays a key role in advancing BCCNM's enterprise data strategy. Working in close collaboration and alignment with the Data Optimization Centre, the position is integral to strengthening Regulatory Policy & Programs' ability to govern, manage, analyze, and use data and content to support regulatory decision-making, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. The position works to establish sustainable practices, standards, governance, and reusable solutions that improve how regulatory data and content is created, managed, shared, and used.

The position works across structured data, such as system fields, measures, reports, and analytics, and unstructured content, including case documents, correspondence, forms, evidence, templates, and knowledge resources. It translates regulatory needs into integrated data, content, reporting, governance, and process improvements while ensuring alignment with privacy, security, records management, and regulatory requirements.

Initially, the position will provide dedicated support and continuity for Professional Conduct Review (PCR) during the period it undergoes Core Regulatory Transformation (CRT). As enterprise and Data Optimization Centre priorities evolve, the position is expected to be assigned to other Regulatory Policy & Programs areas to extend successful practices, build capability, and develop reusable solutions.

Title: Data Analytics & Automation Engineer
Description:
Ready to build data solutions that shape business decisions across Canada?

Passionate about using analytics, automation, and modern data platforms to tackle sophisticated business challenges?

Join Aon and play a key role in transforming how data, reporting, and automation support Commercial Risk operations. This is an exciting chance to define scalable analytics solutions, deliver business insights, and drive innovation through modern data platforms and automation technologies.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. This role is not eligible for sponsorship, and we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa or work permit.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What The Day Will Look Like

As a Data Analytics & Automation Engineer, you will collaborate with business leaders, analytics professionals, operational collaborators, and technology teams. You will deliver scalable reporting, automation, and data solutions that support strategic decision-making. You'll play a meaningful role in developing and managing data platforms, automation technologies, and reporting capabilities that enable the business to operate more efficiently and effectively.

Key Responsibilities Include

Analytics Solution Delivery


Own the build, development, and delivery of enterprise reporting and analytics solutions.
Interpret business requirements and develop scalable technical solutions.
Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and self-service reporting capabilities.
Partner with business leaders to identify reporting opportunities and drive adoption of analytics solutions.
Deliver insights that support data-driven decision making across multiple business functions.


Power Platform Ownership


Design, develop, and maintain Power Apps and Power Automate solutions.
Establish and lead application lifecycle management (ALM) processes across development, testing, and production environments.
Maintain deployment pipelines and solution release processes.
Support governance, security, licensing, and Power Platform guidelines.
Fix sophisticated platform issues and collaborate with Microsoft support where required.


Data Engineering & Platform Management


Support and enhance analytical environments within Databricks and Snowflake.
Design and maintain automated data ingestion, transformation, and integration processes.
Develop and supervise scalable data pipelines.
Improve accessibility and reliability of enterprise data assets.
Support the ongoing enhancement of Aon's Data & Analytics Service Platform (DASP).


Business Process Automation


Find opportunities to streamline and automate manual processes.
Develop enterprise automation solutions using Power Automate and related technologies.
Manage workflows supporting reporting, access provisioning, operational activities, and data management processes.
Ensure all automation solutions align with governance, audit, and security standards.


Dashboard & Reporting Administration


Administer dashboard publishing, distribution, and access management processes.
Support reporting platforms, microsites, and content distribution solutions.
Ensure reporting solutions remain secure, scalable, and reliable.
Coordinate support and ownership transitions for reporting assets.


Customer Engagement & Governance


Partner with operational leaders, broking teams, analytics professionals, and technology customers.
Lead discovery sessions, solution workshops, and project planning activities.
Communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical audiences.
Maintain user documentation, operational procedures, and platform governance standards.
Participate in ongoing platform support and issue resolution activities.


How This Opportunity Is Different

This role sits within a highly transparent and evolving Data & Analytics function supporting Aon's Commercial Risk business across Canada. You'll join a collaborative team that combines business expertise, analytics, and technology to solve real-world challenges and uncover opportunities that drive growth and operational excellence.

Unlike many data-focused roles, you'll have the opportunity to influence the full lifecycle of solutions, from business discovery and customer engagement through to engineering, automation, reporting, and adoption. You'll work alongside data analysts, data scientists, operational leaders, and technology partners while helping shape the future of analytics and automation capabilities across the business.

Skills And Experience That Will Lead To Success


5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, or automation-focused roles.
Experience developing solutions using Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, SQL, and Python.
Hands-on experience with modern data platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, Azure Data Services, or similar technologies.
Solid ability to translate business requirements into adaptable technical architectures and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical customers.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Data Analytics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.


Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.
